💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that designer Claire Thompson has a theory about renovating a house alongside your significant other: If your relationship can survive that, it can probably survive anything.
  • Built in 1964, the five-bedroom property hadn’t been meaningfully upgraded in decades.
  • In a recent development, the decision to stay rather than sell came with a change in approach.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that designer Claire Thompson has a theory about renovating a house alongside your significant other: If your relationship can survive that, it can probably survive anything. In 2021, she and her now-husband, Will, purchased a nearly 5,000-square-foot home in Jackson, Mississippi’s Eastover neighborhood, with plans to renovate the property and flip it for a profit. By 2022, they were engaged in the unfinished kitchen. Four years later, they’re still there, now with a baby daughter and a house that looks very little like the one they originally intended to sell.

Built in 1964, the five-bedroom property hadn’t been meaningfully upgraded in decades. The rooms were compartmentalized, the finishes were dated, and the quirky floor blueprint presented a few head-scratching challenges, like a second-floor dining room entirely removed from the kitchen below. But Thompson, who rolled out her design business in 2020, saw something worth holding onto. “I swiftly fell in love with the bones of the home, the lot the home is positioned on, and of course the neighborhood and the street itself,” she recalls.

In a recent development, the decision to stay rather than sell came with a change in approach. Rather than gutting the house and putting in finishes they knew would grab buyers in a post-COVID market, the couple worked within the home’s existing footprint, opening up walls to encourage better circulation while preserving the individuality of each room. The kitchen, once closed off at either end, now connects to a light-filled breakfast nook and an inviting keeping room, where damaged parquet floors and dated ceiling beams gave way to white oak underfoot and softly textured plaster overhead.

Nearby, a former study became an inky, book-lined library, complete with an expanded bar. Even the upstairs dining room survived, despite its logistical inconveniences. “We decided to keep it because of the way it flows when we entertain and host showers or parties,” Thompson notes. “I think a home that tells a story, like a nod to the past or an interesting quirk, only makes the home more intriguing.”.

It has been revealed that the renovation unfolded after hours, with Will building cabinetry and tackling electrical work late into the night. Some spaces were even renovated twice: first, with resale in mind, then with the more personal considerations of permanence. The home became a testing ground for Thompson’s design practice, but it also serves as something of a family scrapbook. “We grew together as individuals, as a couple, as business owners, and as creatives,” she claims. “The home feels like us.”.

FAST FACTSDesigner: Claire Thompson DesignLocation: Jackson, MississippiThe Space: A five-bedroom, four-and-a-half-bathroom home across 5,000 square feet.

The kitchen layout didn’t change too much, but Thompson was able to completely upgrade its feel and functionality by opening up both ends—one to the breakfast nook, one to the keeping room—and adding a center island.

According to recent reports, “I really did not want upper cabinets in the kitchen, so we were very thoughtful in the functionality of the cabinetry,” she adds. “My husband loves to remind me that he built me 42 drawers for the kitchen. We have ample storage, while still making it aesthetically the way I envisioned.”.

According to recent reports, now open to the kitchen, the breakfast nook acts as a natural overflow spot where the family eats most of their meals, casual dinners included. Removing the ceiling beams allowed Thompson to capture the feel of taller ceilings; while she wanted to keep the brick floors, opening up the walls meant she had to opt for latest white oak for continuity.

In a recent development, “We call this the keeping room since we opened it up to the kitchen,” explains Thompson. “This is the room we really live in day to day; it’s a laid-back and comfortable space.”.

Industry observers note that the pair started by plastering just the fireplace, but then decided to extend the treatment throughout the rest of the room—it’s since become a signature finish for Thompson’s firm. “We now use this technique in almost every project,” she adds.

Previously a study, the library was born of equal parts design instincts and necessity. “My husband has so many books that we decided to wrap the room with bookshelves,” explains Thompson, who also reworked a hallway to add a bar and powder bathroom. The whole space is drenched in a Roman clay finish (Black Star by Portola Paints), creating an enveloping retreat that has become a go-to for family movie nights.

In a recent development, also known as the family’s “Christmas tree room,” the formal living room is a soothing symphony of neutral hues and nubby textures. “The coffee table is one of my favorite purchases of all time,” Thompson adds. “I bought it to sell to a client but decided I couldn’t part with it! I also love to have my grandmother’s antique stool in here—it always makes me think of her and brings me joy.”.

In a recent development, perfectly balanced between sweet and sophisticated, 12-week-old daughter Margot’s bedroom was an opportunity for Thompson to lean into all things childhood magic. “She may never leave the bassinet in our primary bedroom, but she does have a cute room waiting for her if that ever happens!” she adds.

Sources indicate that connected to the nursery through a Jack-and-Jill bathroom, this guest space could eventually become a bedroom for a second child. For now, though, it’s a comfortable spot for visiting guests, and a favorite hideout of Thompson’s “first baby,” pup Lemmon.

Claire Thompson is the owner of Claire Thompson Design, a full-service firm specializing in designing, renovating, and furnishing beautiful, timeless homes. She works closely with clients to ensure their unique personalities and desires are perfectly captured by the design and that all their wishes and needs are met.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What sets The Altruists apart from other limited series about millennial scammers in the 2010s is a love story between two like-minded individuals who just *got* each other’s quirks, habits, and Harry Potter fandom. Sure, the relationship between Sam Bankman-Fried (Anthony Boyle) and Caroline Ellison (Julia Garner) was a contributing factor to their corporate failure and fraudulent activities. But it’s compelling. And, in a time where geeky pursuits are increasingly under the microscope, The Altruists presents the most mature and romantic view of erotic fan fiction that we’ve seen in a while.

It has been revealed that early on in The Altruists, Sam discovers that Caroline reads and writes explicit Draco/Hermione fan fiction. (Because television is a visual medium Caroline also prints her story out, which is odd. Not a bad idea, though, given recent events.) He laughs nervously at first, but then reacts positively. “This is hot,” he insists. “You know what you like. You know how to express yourself. You know what turns you on. And you can talk about it. I think you’re incredible. I think you’re so cool.”.

Holy nuance, Batman! Why does a 23-year-old MIT grad have a less judgmental take on erotica than half of the think pieces I’ve read over the last 2 to 3 years? Yes, exploring fantasies and kinks and learning how to express them in a safe environment are some of the many positives about fan fiction and/or romance as a genre. This opinion is surprisingly mature for a guy who wants to turn finance into a video game, dresses like Mark Zuckerberg’s kid brother, communicates via memes, and almost exclusively hires his childhood friends. Granted, in the moment he wants to impress Caroline, and The Altruists is not a documentary. But it goes to show that, when it comes to nerdy things, you really do have to ask a nerd.

Sources indicate that the real Ellison is a well-documented Harry Potter fan and a LARPer. According to the NY Post, she wrote a regency romance novel while awaiting sentencing. Fortune’s profile of Ellison includes her original fantasy writing. Gawker went ham on Ellison’s Tumblr and found a link to Gossip Girl fan fiction. You can skim an archive of an archive of those Tumblr posts and see references to Lore Olympus, the fic “Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality,” posts comparing herself to Hermione, and more... but no real evidence that she posted to FF.net or AO3 herself.

The Altruists is fiction land. Not every character shares Sam’s tolerant views, sadly. When Caroline’s coworkers find the story, cheekily titled “A Ride On Draco’s Nimbus,” they make fun of her. Anticipating that she’ll no longer be taken seriously at pitch meetings, she quits. This frees her up to start working with Sam, who again assures her that he doesn’t find her writing fan fiction embarrassing. Later, one of the only other female employees at FTX mocks Caroline behind her back.

But in The Altruists finale, when the press tries to expose Caroline’s “controversial” writing, Sam shuts them down in a televised interview.

Sources indicate that I’m just going to say it: that line is so romantic. It’s such an ingenious choice to have a public defense of writing fan fiction serve as Sam’s final declaration of love on The Altruists. He says it direct to camera, as if he knows Caroline is watching. That’s how he expresses to her, and the world, that he still cares about her. You know what else is hot? Having a moral line you refuse to cross, no matter what happens.

In a recent development, also, in the words of terminally online millennials everywhere, he’s right and he should say it! As the fan-fiction-to-novel-to-screen adaptation pipeline (the After series, The Love Hypothesis, Game Changers AKA Kip and Scott’s book from Heated Rivalry, etc.) pushes the form into the mainstream, outsider efforts to understand fan fiction’s pull unfortunately tend to further “other” it. Even calling something a guilty pleasure still implies that it’s something one should feel shame about. When headlines about fan fiction open with “Why Are You So Into This” and “Celebrities Reveal How They Really Feel” the clear negative connotation hangs above the most positive arguments. What if we didn’t do that?

In a recent development, throughout the series, The Altruists will occasionally show Caroline self-inserting as Hermione through the fic that she writes. It’s not framed in a way that makes her look especially silly or childish. It just tells the audience how she’s feeling about Draco Sam at any given time, simple as that. It’s a creative outlet! Maybe we should, and I can’t believe I’m saying this, be more like Sam Bankman-Fried*.

Unfortunately, I’m not even sure we can prove Dramione is Ellison’s Harry Potter OTP IRL. Pity, because Boyle originated the role of Draco’s bookish son Scorpius Malfoy in the play Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. What better meta silver lining could a convicted felon fangirl ask for? She needs it, too, because I don’t think the real Bankman-Fried defended her like that either. Bummer.

It has been revealed that *A fictional version of Sam Bankman-Fried, written by Graham Moore and portrayed by Boyle in The Altruists, a work of fiction. Don’t get it twisted!

For some context: The Jamaican-born reality star hurled this insult at fellow cast member Amanda Cronin, noting that—while Karen “came to England at 25 years old” and now owns “five properties”—Amanda sleeps with princes, lords, and mayors and still only has “one mews house.” Please give it a watch, if you haven’t already.

Recent findings suggest that while RHOLDN is the third UK installment of The Real Housewives franchise, it’s the first original series for Hayu, with season 1 only becoming available to stream on Bravo in the U.S. in July 2026 (nearly a year after its August 2025 debut on Hayu). But after the mega-virality of that season 2 reunion clip, RHOLDN will almost certainly get a season 3...and it definitely has Bravo’s attention.

Industry observers note that it’s unclear whether a potential season 3 could air on Bravo in real time alongside Hayu, but what is clear is that RHOLDN is a force to be reckoned with, especially as other Real Housewives franchises are starting to lose their relevancy. (Please see: Real Housewives of Orange County.) And the “low-budget vagina” read isn’t the first time that RHOLDN has delivered a meme-able moment, either. Remember Amanda’s “Back to Paddington” clapback from season 1?

So...what does this mean about the future of RHOLDN (which, as a reminder, hasn’t yet been renewed for season 3)? According to The Sun, production is reportedly looking to shake up the cast to bring even more stars who can deliver drama like Karen.

“Karen has really set the bar for what they’re looking for,” a source claimed. “She’s got the personality, the lifestyle, and that larger-than-life presence that makes brilliant television. They’re keen to find another one or two women who can go toe-to-toe with someone like Karen, rather than fade into the background.”.

What’s more: “Nothing is set in stone, but there’s definitely a feeling that the next series needs to be bigger, bolder, and a little less polite.”.

According to recent reports, could this fan interest also mean that Bravo’s Ladies of London reboot gets taken off pause? No word on that yet, but a girl can dream!

In a recent development, are you ready for your annual awkward family gathering? Thanksgiving is finally here, and if thinking about safe topics to discuss with all three generations of your family is making you break out in hives, then rest assured we’ve got some recipes to give you the liquid courage to face it.

You’ve got the turkey basted and roasting in the oven. You’ve got your grandmother’s perfect mac and cheese. You’ve got mashed potatoes—the best. And you’ve got store-bought pie from your slacker cousin. But, wait, do you know what you’ll be drinking for the most important feast of the year? We promise: There’s something for everyone at your dinner table on this curated list of cocktails.

It has been revealed that does Grandpa only abide by the saying, “If it’s brown, drink it down?” We’ve got a few whiskey drinks that will keep him on ice. Did your aunt who drinks only French reds run through the bottle she brought already? There’s a sangria recipe that’ll have her too busy sipping to snip. Need a warm cup of something strong while you “take the dog for a walk”? There’s an Irish coffee that’ll keep your wits about you. So hurry up and add these cocktail recipes to your Turkey Day menu.

Here’s a whiskey sour that makes your fall-flavor dreams come true.

Add ingredients to a shaker and shake without ice. Pour into a glass and garnish with grated nutmeg and a dried apple slice.

This twist on the old-fashioned adds an autumnal flavor that will keep this classic feeling fresh.

According to recent reports, combine all ingredients into a mixing glass with ice. Stir until chilled and diluted. Strain into a rocks glass with a large cube. Garnish with an orange peel studded with cloves.

The delicious spice that goes into a pie doesn’t have to be just for lattes or baked goods.

Cover the rim of a stemless wineglass in simple syrup. Dip in cinnamon sugar and add ice to the glass. Pour in pumpkin-spice liqueur and Josh Cellars sauvignon blanc. Stir, then top off the glass with seltzer.

This three-ingredient cocktail is easy to whip up but will taste like it was complicated and time-consuming.

Recent findings suggest that mix cider and cinnamon whiskey in a Champagne flute. Top with Champagne, then stir lightly until incorporated. Garnish with an apple slice.

A sweet, fizzy sipper to enjoy before dinner.

It has been revealed that add all liquid ingredients to a stemless wineglass. Add ice. Stir to incorporate, then garnish.

A roasty, toasty espresso martini to enjoy after the big dinner.

Shake ingredients hard with ice until frothy, about 15 seconds. Double-strain into a chilled coupe or martini glass. Garnish with coffee beans, nutmeg, and cinnamon.

This sumptuous hot cocktail makes a great Thanksgiving treat.

In a mug, dissolve the sugar cubes in a little hot water. Add rum and butter. Fill the mug with hot water. Sprinkle nutmeg on top.

The margarita isn’t just a summer drink anymore.

It has been revealed that in a cocktail shaker, combine all the ingredients with ice and shake. Rim a glass with cinnamon sugar and serve over rocks. Garnish with slices of lime and orange.

You need to keep the booze flowing to keep the mood light and the conversation going. So mix together this sangria recipe that’ll satiate any apple-cider lover.

Place apples, orange, and cloves in a large pitcher. Drizzle honey over the fruit, then add in apple cider, rum, ginger beer, and white wine. Stir to mix. Top with ice and let chill for 20 minutes before serving. Serve in glasses, including the chunks of fruit.

Whoever invented pouring bourbon into a cup of tea, we want to give you a major hug.

Boil water in a teapot. Steep star anise pod or tea bag inside. Add bourbon, honey, lemon, and Tiki bitters to a mug. Stir. Serve in glass mugs with a spoon and the teapot. To enjoy, pour tea over cocktail base to taste and stir.

This aperitivo is the perfect refreshment before you start serving those heavy Thanksgiving dishes.

Recent findings suggest that pour Campari and sweet vermouth into a highball glass filled with ice. Top with club soda. Garnish with an orange twist.

A balanced spin on the Manhattan that uses Scotch whisky, this cocktail will impress any fan of brown liquor.

In a recent development, stir the Scotch, vermouth, and bitters well with cracked ice. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass. Garnish with a lemon twist.

Simple enough to whip up in under five minutes, this cocktail has enough Scotch to knock Grandpa under the table.

In a recent development, stir the Scotch and amaretto well with cracked ice in a mixing glass. Strain over fresh ice into an old-fashioned glass.

If you’re a big fan of cranberry sauce (the one that comes in a can), you can cure your cranberry craving with this vodka cocktail.

It has been revealed that shake ingredients in a shaker with cracked ice. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, then garnish with lime.

This green-tinged cocktail tastes fresh and slightly tart, but it’s boozy enough to chill you out after that heavy holiday meal.

Add all ingredients into a shaker. Shake well with cracked ice. Strain into a coupe glass. Garnish with a lime wedge and Luxardo cherries.

The Black Russian is the espresso martini’s cooler, more laid-back cousin. It’s so simple to make and yet deliciously complex in taste.

Recent findings suggest that stir ingredients with ice in a mixing glass. Strain into an old-fashioned glass over fresh ice.

In a recent development, sometimes you don’t want to have to choose between two options, because you want to have it all! And you can have it both ways, with this gin-and-vodka martini, the vesper.

According to recent reports, stir ingredients briskly with ice in a mixing tin until very cold. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass. Garnish with a large, thin-cut lemon peel.

According to recent reports, why not turn your holiday gathering into an international experience? Incorporate this Russian classic into your cocktail rotation.

Squeeze lime juice into a copper mug (or a Collins glass) and drop in the spent hull. Add ice cubes, then pour in the vodka and fill with cold ginger beer. Serve with a stirring rod.

One of my favorite ways to wear a chunky knit sweater is over a flowing mini dress and paired with knee-high riding boots (more on that next). For a preppier take, I slip on cigarette jeans, tube socks, and soft loafers.

Falconeri Ultrasoft Cashmere Funnel Neck Sweater.

Versace Signature Cat-Eye Sunglasses.

Anthropologie Minimal Claw Clips.

But once I secured the Aritzia Jones Bomber Leather Jacket in burnt brown, I became an exclusive coffee-colored jacket wearer.

It has been revealed that the warm, chocolatey hue effortlessly pairs with fall’s color palette, including wine red, golden ochre, and mossy green. And it feels a little more relaxed than a classic black biker style. Whether I’m wearing a sophisticated silk slip dress or casual low-slung jeans, I know my mocha leather jacket will be the perfect top layer for the occasion.

Aritzia Falcon Jacket - UnReal Leather.

Levi's Faux Leather Relaxed Fit Bomber.

Abercrombie Vegan Leather Bubble Hem Coat.

Pacsun Faux Leather Bomber Jacket.

I love pairing my moto footwear with color-blocked barn jackets, houndstooth mini skirts, and oversized blazers. We all know design is reflective. Whether it’s in our personal style, architectural splendor, or cultural ties, great design mirrors the world around us. Now, it’s time for it to mirror itself.

According to recent reports, once dismissed as a tacky, ’70s-era trend (not unlike wood paneling), mirrored surfaces are making a comeback. But don’t worry—today’s mirror craze moves past the floor-to-ceiling panels of the past, opting instead for accents that add light, depth, and dimension.

According to recent reports, “I love mirrored surfaces in interiors because they can be so transformative & work in all styles. They can add glitz and glamour, especially when you add beveled details,” states Bridget Tiek of TIEK BYDAY. “I love to see mirrors as a backbar, behind shelves, on doors, ceilings and on walls. Basically everywhere!”.

Sources indicate that bolder than traditional ready-to-hang mirrors, mirrored surfaces are often hard to place tastefully. Here’s how designers have brought the striking detail into interiors.

Sources indicate that queer Eye for the Straight Guy star Carson Kressley’s Murray Hill apartment is full of personality, and his sunken living room has several glittering surfaces. The designer embraces mirrored shine as a bold accent, as seen in this disco-ball-tiled end table.

Use It for a Bold Bar Backsplash.

Recent findings suggest that designer Alexander D. Wilson brought a mirrored backsplash into this Upper East Side apartment to elevate the elegant yet fun palette while creating the illusion of a larger space. NYC apartments often feel like a shoebox. With this classic design trick, they don’t have to look like it.

Interior designer Sarah Vaile brought Manhattan to the Windy City in this punchy coastal home. After coating the walls in Farrow & Ball’s Borrowed Light for a classic Nancy Meyers-esque aesthetic, she framed a nearly ceiling-high mirror in crisp white molding, transforming the panel into a bold decorative piece that amplifies space and cosmopolitan chic.

Incorporate as a Tasteful Touch.

Bold enough to make a fierce statement in even the smallest piece, interior designer Amy Courtney brought industrial flair to her Newly introduced York City home with a silvery domed lamp to complement the bold hues of her living room’s palette.

While the glassy, expansive nature of mirrored panels certainly has its charms, if you’re hoping to bring both glossy and textured flair to your design, mirrored tiles are the perfect solution. Designer Shannon Ggem used mirrored tiles in this moody bar design to bring more light to the room without sacrificing the deep-hued palette.

While most rely on millwork to bring style to the walls, designer Michelle Prentice opted for mirror panels on the closet doors of this South Carolina bedroom. Not only do they add depth to the design, but they bring a boutique feel while adding to the visual palette and playing off the centered vanity mirror to unify the wall treatments.

Recent findings suggest that as stainless steel fades from an industry standard to a passing fad, designers are getting creative when it comes to finding chic alternatives. In this monochrome green butler’s pantry, designer Bridget Tiek brought in a glassy paneled door to elevate the appliance design, taking the invisible kitchen trend to new heights.

I'm a Mom of Two, and This Ernesta Rug Gives Me That Luxe Look With the Easy Cleanup of a Washable Option

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1377 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor.
  • According to recent reports, I have to admit, I have a bit of a gripe with washable rugs.
  • In a recent development, while washable rug options have definitely improved over the years, there’s still something about the weight, texture, and character of a traditional rug that I find hard to forgo for the sake of washability.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

According to recent reports, I have to admit, I have a bit of a gripe with washable rugs. For years, the design industry has been trying to convince us that the answer to a beautiful, livable home is a washable rug. And while I understand the appeal, especially as a mom to two young kids, a dog, and a household that sees its fair share of spills, muddy shoes, and general chaos, I’ve just never been entirely sold on the idea.

In a recent development, while washable rug options have definitely improved over the years, there’s still something about the weight, texture, and character of a traditional rug that I find hard to forgo for the sake of washability. I want a rug that feels substantial underfoot, looks better with age, and doesn’t require me to wrestle an eight-by-ten-foot piece of fabric into my washing machine every time someone spills a juice box.

Sources indicate that when I learned about Ernesta’s protective rug treatment, I was intrigued. The custom rug brand offers an optional treatment designed to help repel spills and make everyday messes easier to clean, without requiring you to compromise on your rug’s style, material, or size. In theory, it offers the best of both worlds: the look and feel of a beautifully made rug, with a little extra insurance against the realities of family life. Plus, it’s a treatment that’s typically hard to access on your own without going custom through a designer.

It has been revealed that I actually have several Ernesta rugs in my home (I’m a huge fan of their quality and approachable customization options!), but after swapping in an Ernesta rug treated with the brand’s protective finish in our living room, I don’t think I’ll ever go back to ordering a rug without it. Here’s what you should know about the treatment, how it's held up in my own home, and why I think it may be a smarter investment than yet another washable rug.

Best for: This rug is an excellent option for families, pet owners, or anyone who just prefers not to have to be too precious with their things.

Not ideal for: Anyone looking for a quick-ship rug option.

Bottom Line: The customization of Ernesta’s rug assortment makes it easy to get the exact look and function that serves your home best, including different sizes, non-slip bases, and protections.

One of the reasons I love Ernesta so much is how approachable they make the ordering process. There’s no visiting a showroom or making 400 phone calls to try to get the right custom-cut size. You simply log on to their site, browse the options, then choose up to five samples to try for just $10.

My samples came incredibly swiftly—within a few days, they were at my doorstep, ready for review. Because I already liked the look of the rug we had in our living room (more on that later), I knew I didn’t want to stray too far from the neutral, functional foundation it gave us.

Sources indicate that when we started, we had Ernesta’s Emerson sisal rug in the space. The nubby texture and color looked beautiful, but it was a bit small (it was originally sized to an old home that we have since moved from), and the deeper grooves of the weave made it hard to clean up spills. I have two young kids and a dog, and truly not a day goes by where someone hasn’t spilled yogurt or cracker crumbs or juice on the rug.

In a recent development, still, I don’t think you should have to sacrifice beauty for function in a family home, and Ernesta helped us find that balance. After debating between a few different styles, I ended up settling on the Cally wool flatweave rug in Camel. Wool flatweave rugs are notoriously durable on their own, and I knew the protective coating would only help it hold up better. Bonus: The tighter weave meant fewer nooks and crannies for gunk to get into.

It has been revealed that once we decided on our fresh style, we measured out the size we’d need, which ended up being around 13 x 15 feet. I loved how easy it was to order the exact size we needed for our space, especially given that it wasn’t a standard measurement. If you’re unsure about the right size for your rug (or how many legs of your furniture should be on the rug at one time), Ernesta has helpful guidance on their site.

Placing the order was easy; you can opt into the protective treatment before adding the order to your cart, as well as choose other details, like the type of edge binding and whether you’d like to include a rug pad (we chose the attached version).

Sources indicate that protective treatments for rugs are nothing new; they’ve been available to design industry insiders for years. That stated, very few DTC companies offer the treatment, unless you’re buying through a designer or want to seek out a supplier on your own.

That’s what’s so great about Ernesta’s offerings—it’s literally as easy as checking a box before you add your rug to cart. The treatment starts at $62 and increases depending on the size of your rug. Their formula is non-toxic and works by acting as a protective layer between the surface of the rug and any spills or debris, preventing stains from setting in and keeping the fibers intact for longer.

Receiving and installing our Ernesta rug couldn’t have been easier, especially considering its large size. It was delivered and placed in our entryway, where it waited for a few days until my husband and I had a spare moment to lay it out.

According to recent reports, the rug was packaged beautifully, with thick plastic wrapping protecting the roll, a firm cardboard tube at the center, and fabric wrapping the edges so the binding didn’t get roughed up in transit. I thought this was a particularly nice touch.

Sources indicate that as with most rugs, the corners were a bit flared when we first unrolled it, so here’s my favorite tip: add several ice cubes to any corner you want to lay flat and let them melt. The slow dissipation of moisture will relax the rug's fibers, and by the time it has melted away completely, you should have a totally flat rug.

I was immediately impressed by the look and feel of this rug—the wool was so soft and plush, and the rubber mat integrated on the bottom meant it did not budge once we laid it down (though it did make it difficult to reposition when we laid it a little wonky initially, word to the wise). There was no “chemical” smell from the protective treatments, and the fibers still felt just as soft as they did on the sample I received before ordering.

Industry observers note that aesthetically, I love the vibe that this rug brings to the space. It’s soft and plush and cozy, and finally in better proportion with the rest of the room—which is great, because I have a pair of armchairs I won at auction waiting in the wings for their moment. Before, they were floating off the rug and looked odd, but now, they’ll be perfect.

Logically, the protective treatment was 100 percent the right choice for our family. Not even five minutes after laying it out, my three-year-old squished an applesauce pouch on the rug, and it came up with ease. In the month since having it, we’ve definitely put this rug through the paces of family life, and it still looks as good as the day we opened it. Cleaning it is easy, and Ernesta has a whole page on their site dedicated to care instructions, depending on the material your rug is made of.

Overall, this is the ideal solution to me: a rug that looks as good as it performs, and doesn’t require any design sacrifice (or yelling from mom) in the process.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando are officially married! Nearly one year after their engagement was confirmed, the couple tied the knot on Saturday, November 21, in Palm Springs, California.

The singer, who said “I do” in Saint Laurent, shared black-and-white photos from the wedding on Instagram, simply captioning the post, “M+M 🤍 11.21.26.” In photos, the couple could be seen exchanging vows in a poolside ceremony featuring a stunning display of sweeping white flowers and candles.

In a recent development, in December 2025, Cyrus confirmed her engagement to musician Maxx Morando—a relationship she has largely kept out of the spotlight following her highly publicized marriage to Liam Hemsworth. The Bass Persuades singer was first linked to Morando in November 2021, when the two sparked romance rumors with a joint appearance at the Gucci Love Parade fashion show. (Cyrus later shared a photo of herself with Morando from the event on Instagram.).

Sources indicate that rumors escalated the following month, when Cyrus danced and held hands with Morando in Miami during her New Year’s Eve Party special for NBC. By April 2022, they confirmed their romance during an outing in West Hollywood, where they went all out with the PDA.

Fast forward to the 2024 Grammys and Morando supported Cyrus at the show—where she won her first Grammy for “Flowers”—and he gave her a passionate kiss.

In a recent development, since then, the two have kept their relationship low-key aside from a few red carpet appearances together. But while Morando has mostly kept his personal life out of the public spotlight, he, like Cyrus, has had a long career in music.

Ahead, everything we know about Cyrus’s newly introduced husband, Maxx Morando.

While best known as the drummer for Liily (and for the Regrettes, from 2015 to 2018), Morando also plays guitar. Additionally, he has also collaborated with Cyrus on several of her albums, including her most recent release, Bass Persuades. For the project, he co-produced the album’s title track alongside Cyrus, as well as several others, including “Aftermath” and “REDLIGHTS.” The musician also has songwriting credits, co-writing “Innocent Ways” with Cyrus and being credited on “Aftermath.”.

Morando also produced two songs, “Handstand” and “Violet Chemistry,” from the singer’s Endless Summer Vacation LP.

Sources indicate that he also collaborated with Cyrus on her 2025 album, Something Beautiful, contributing as both a producer and songwriter on several tracks. Morando also played drums on the record and made a cameo in the “End of the World” music video.

The drummer, born in 1998, is six years Cyrus’s junior. (His birthday also happens to fall exactly a week ahead of the singer’s, on November 16.).

Cyrus opened up about their slight age gap in a 2024 interview with Harper’s Bazaar: “He grew up with a laptop. I had a desktop computer that I shared with my brothers and sisters. … Honestly, he’s raised our dog off Reddit. I’m like, Are you sure we’re supposed to be doing this? And he’s like, On Reddit it says blah, blah, blah.”.

Along with his musical endeavors, the drummer has dabbled in fashion design too, with Cyrus as his muse.

Cyrus revealed in September 2021 that Morando contributed cartoon designs to a custom vegan leather set by designer Shane Kastl, which Cyrus wore for a performance that month.

Recent findings suggest that “This look is a one-of-a-kind collaboration between two of my favorite emerging artists, Maxx Morando and Shane Kastl,” Cyrus remarked of the special look in an interview. “Their collaboration is the perfect example of sustainability becoming the next fashion phase, and it proves that anything can be reinvented, which resonates with me deeply.”.

Sources indicate that in an interview for Bazaar’s December 2024 cover story, Cyrus opened up about her relationship with Morando, saying, “He’s very similar to me. We just don’t take life too seriously.”.

She also shared how working with Morando on musical projects helped them bond: “I worked with my dad forever. That’s how me and my ex-husband met each other. I’ve always worked with the people that I love,” Cyrus claims. “And Maxx just inspires me so much.”.

The couple’s engagement was confirmed in December 2025, after Cyrus sparked rumors by wearing a diamond sparkler on her left-hand ring finger at the premiere of Avatar: Fire and Ash in LA.

In a recent development, morando keeps an extremely private, low profile in both his personal and professional life. While the musician does have an Instagram, he rarely posts, aside from sharing latest music that he works on with both his band and Cyrus.

In March 2023, a source told People that Morando is a “cool guy” who is drama-free, a trait that Cyrus finds extremely attractive.

It has been revealed that “He has no interest in being a huge celebrity; he’s very low-key. Miley loves these qualities,” the source said. “Miley can be herself. They are supportive of each other’s careers. Miley is enjoying life and things are great.”.

It has been revealed that following a year-long engagement, the Morando and Cyrus officially wed in an intimate ceremony held in Palm Springs, California. The couple shared photos from the wedding on Instagram, which included black-and-white portraits of the couple with their dog, as well as a sweet photo of them kissing after saying “I do.”.

For the ceremony, the bride wore a long-sleeve, backless Saint Laurent wedding gown, while Morando kept things classic in a black suit.

The poolside ceremony took place at Frank Sinatra’s former home, which was transformed with hundreds of white roses for the occasion. In photos obtained by DeuxMoi, the couple could be seen exchanging vows by the pool, in front of an intimate crowd of guests dressed in all-black attire.

Louis Vuitton Takes Its Place at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix Finish Line

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (373 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Elle

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Max Verstappen crossed the finish line at the Las Vegas Formula 1 Grand Prix on Saturday night, after a gripping race that saw the championship driver battle to maintain the tightest of leads against rivals George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, his trophy came in very special packaging: a bespoke Louis Vuitton trunk.
  • The Las Vegas trunk was, like all Louis Vuitton custom pieces, made at Asnières-sur-Seine, a commune in northern France.
  • It has been revealed that louis Vuitton’s relationship with Formula 1 began with the Grand Prix de Monaco, which the brand began creating Trophy Trunks for in 2021.

When Max Verstappen crossed the finish line at the Las Vegas Formula 1 Grand Prix on Saturday night, after a gripping race that saw the championship driver battle to maintain the tightest of leads against rivals George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, his trophy came in very special packaging: a bespoke Louis Vuitton trunk. For the past two seasons, Trophy Trunks have been presented to the winner of the annual Las Vegas event, which sees drivers race on a thrilling course that winds along the famous Strip. They have also been presented to the winners of the World Cup, America’s Cup, and the NBA Finals. Louis Vuitton had a strong presence across the whole race weekend, hosting a suite where guests including Teyana Taylor watched the events from above the track and were able to get an early look at the trunk.

The Las Vegas trunk was, like all Louis Vuitton custom pieces, made at Asnières-sur-Seine, a commune in northern France. It was handcrafted by 25 artisans, made to the specific dimensions of the trophy. The Trophy Trunks are a remarkable mingling of the old and the new. They use the traditional craftsmanship techniques that have defined the house for over 170 years. All construction of the trunks’ wood, leather, and locks was done with the same techniques LV has used since the beginning, meaning that in many ways the Trophy Trunks differ little from its trunks from a century ago. The modern energy of motor racing comes through via subtle touches like the two stripes across the trunk that make a large V, a nod to both Vuitton and victory—they’re black-and-white checkered as a nod to the Formula 1 finish line. A small badge that calls back to the early days of trunk travel and bears the winning driver’s initials was added this year.

It has been revealed that louis Vuitton’s relationship with Formula 1 began with the Grand Prix de Monaco, which the brand began creating Trophy Trunks for in 2021. In 2025, it became an official partner of the league, and this year, LV created trunks for all 24 of the season’s races. In early December, the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix will mark the final 2026 race.

Recent findings suggest that on this outing, Gabbriette kept it understated, pairing her simple black dress with a set of leather ballet flats, a chunky bracelet, and a quilted top-handle tote bag from Chanel. Healy, meanwhile, wore a gray tee and distressed jeans with gray boots and a navy zip-up jacket.

Recent findings suggest that the couple tied the knot in Los Angeles this past summer, at the Castillo del Lago mansion in Hollywood Hills. Sources indicate that since you’re probs wondering how this couple came to be (and what led to their rumored breakup), I’ve done the work of rounding up all of their biggest relationship moments in a little timeline for your pleasure. Read it and weep!

It has been revealed that ben hard releases their relationship on Instagram by sneaking a photo of Trinity kissing his cheek into a carousel post. Swipe to the end to see:.

Soon after, Trinity clears up some of the discourse around her and Ben’s relationship—namely the story behind how they actually met—and makes a point to note that Frances Tiafoe, a friend of hers and Ben’s, did not introduce them to each other like he previously claimed.

“I can assure you Frances was not the reason we met or got together,” she said in an interview with ESPN. “I don’t know why he’s taking credit for that. Me and Ben can both cut that out. It was a solely me and Ben thing.”.

Recent findings suggest that for the record, their story went a little like this: “I was like, ‘Hey, when you gonna come visit me?’ and he was like, ‘I’ll come right now,’” Trinity explained in an Instagram video (below). “So then he flew out and the rest is history.”.

Ben gives Trinity prime placement on his feed with a super cute photo:.

A few weeks later, Ben wishes Trinity a happy birthday on his Instagram page with a simple but sweet message that reads, “happy birthday beautiful girl, I love you.” Awwwww.

Trinity is spotted in the stands with Ben’s family at Wimbledon.

Recent findings suggest that trinity roots for Ben on day one of the 2025 U.S. Open Tennis Championships, and literally pops out in the cutest ‘fit that consists of Ben’s face plastered all over her custom sweats.

It has been revealed that trinity writes the sweetest tribute message for Ben’s 24th birthday: “To the most beautiful soul I’ve ever met. Happy birthday Benny! Ben and Trinity’s relationship becomes wedding-guest official! The couple gets all gussied up for a friend’s wedding, and they look so good, it’s literally unfair.

Years of Being a Private Investigator Taught Me So Much About Dating Men

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
  • In a recent development, years before he became “Dirty John,” an infamous stalker who preyed on a young woman while carrying a butcher knife hidden in a Del Taco bag, I met John Meehan over dinner at the Chateau Marmont.
  • Sources indicate that it was 2010, and my friend Kate had recently met a handsome, charming anesthesiologist named John Meehan on a dating website.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

In a recent development, years before he became “Dirty John,” an infamous stalker who preyed on a young woman while carrying a butcher knife hidden in a Del Taco bag, I met John Meehan over dinner at the Chateau Marmont. He was dating my friend.

Sources indicate that it was 2010, and my friend Kate had recently met a handsome, charming anesthesiologist named John Meehan on a dating website. She was smitten. He was successful, attentive, and apparently desperate to commit. He'd even asked for a key to her house. Kate was head over heels; I was spooked. Something about John didn't add up.

In a recent development, over dinner, John talked endlessly about his medical career, including the technical details of surgeries with gas ratios and how much money he made. Yet when I asked which medical school he'd attended, he became strangely evasive. When the bill arrived, John meticulously calculated his share down to the penny, despite having spent the evening boasting about his seven-figure income. Maybe he was just frugal. But there was a growing collection of little things that didn't make sense.

Kate thought I was being cynical. At the time, I was an investigative journalist and former sex columnist living in L.A. who had recently enrolled in private investigator school. So, sure, maybe that wasn’t too misplaced. But I trust my instincts and genuinely thought she was in danger—when John left the restaurant, I borrowed my then-husband's Mercedes and followed him. John had told Kate he lived with his sister in Pasadena. He drove somewhere else entirely.

Over the following days, I began digging. I discovered that John wasn't the doctor he claimed to be—he was a nurse anesthetist with a long criminal history, had lost his professional license, and had been accused of stalking women.

I had mixed feelings about telling Kate the truth. I knew that I had to break the bad news, but I was super nervous when I showed up to our happy hour date carrying a printout of John’s mug shot. Fortunately, she believed me and broke things off. And although I suspected at the time that he was a con artist with a serious capacity for violence, I was left feeling helpless.

Sources indicate that years later, I listened in horror as the Dirty John podcast chronicled what happened when John Meehan entered his wife Debra Newell’s life. Their story mirrored his and Kate’s, except that when she tried to break up with him, things took a much darker turn. He eventually attacked her adult daughter, Terra Newell, who bravely fought back and killed him in self-defense. Hearing that, I was relieved that Kate had escaped. But I was also haunted by the knowledge that recognizing a dangerous man hadn't stopped him from finding another victim.

From sitting outside no-tell motels on matrimonial surveillance to piecing together a crime victim’s last day on earth, I’ve seen many situations where people get into dangerous situations—from confronting love rivals to going back for one last suitcase—all for love.

Here’s what detective work has taught me about dating:.

Before I became a private investigator, I was a sex and dating columnist for The Independent in London. I spent years documenting my romantic adventures, writing about everything from casual sex to heartbreak. I've always been fascinated by the similarities between dating and detective work.

Sources indicate that in both instances, you’re sitting across from a relative stranger. You’re asking questions, and you’re trying to figure out whether they are telling the truth—all the while hoping that, in the dating realm, any skeletons you unearth are metaphorical, and not decomposing in someone’s crawlspace.

Sources indicate that but there's one enormous difference. When I'm investigating someone professionally, I'm looking for inconsistencies. When I'm falling for someone, I'm looking for reasons to believe them. And that's where things get dangerous.

It’s been scientifically proven that love causes a dopamine reaction in the brain similar to eating pounds of chocolate or snorting cocaine. Think about it: Would you make any other major life decision—like who to live with, introduce to your children or combine finances with—while high? That’s why I love the idea of a “sexual sober friend,” aka someone who will tell you straight up if you are being totally irrational. Of course, you have to actually be willing to take stated friend’s advice–see below!

One of the most useful lessons I learned in PI school was to not to “give people the benefit of the doubt.” Instead, we say, “Trust, but verify.”.

Recent findings suggest that when you're investigating a crime, you build a timeline. You figure out what happened, when it happened, and whether the evidence supports the accounts you've been given. I think romantic relationships benefit from a much less obsessive version of the same principle.

Someone tells you they're looking for a serious relationship. Do their actions support that statement? Do they make plans? Follow through? Introduce you to people in their lives? Respect your boundaries? Or do they deliver a spectacular speech about wanting to find their soulmate and then disappear for eleven days because, apparently, their phone fell into the sea? A charming explanation is not the same thing as a credible one.

I once worked on a surveillance case involving a wife whose husband worked a boring day job as a dentist...but she was never allowed to come to his office, and he would disappear for hours in the evening. When he told her that he wanted a divorce and was leaving, she wanted to know where he was going, so she hired me and my partner.

After 18 hours of surveillance, I was able to confirm what six years of couples’ therapy had failed to deliver: confirmation that not only was he cheating on her with his receptionist, which I captured on camera while hiding in a deserted parking lot, but that he was leading a double life as a wannabee-Soprano small-time strip club drug dealer.

The next day, as I played the video evidence of his double life, writing prescriptions for several dancers, smoking pot, and shopping the aisles of Trader Joe’s for munchies, she told me that she had suspected for years that something was off, but she never felt ready to ask him the questions that would shatter her world. That’s happened to me a lot when I was doing matrimonial surveillance: People will tell me about finding incriminating photographs, suspicious messages, or underwear that clearly doesn't belong to them—and then ask me whether I think something is wrong.

Often, they're not really asking me to uncover the truth. They're asking me to give them permission to believe what they've already seen. Which brings me to my next principle:.

I believe in intuition, but I don’t believe that it’s supernatural magic. Sometimes it's simply our brains recognizing patterns before we've consciously identified them.

Recent findings suggest that at that first dinner with John Meehan, I couldn't immediately explain why I felt uncomfortable. But as the evening continued, I used my investigative training to spot the inconsistencies: his evasiveness, his elaborate claims, the mismatch between the person he presented and the details of his life. The notable part wasn't that I had a bad feeling, it was that I paid attention to the feeling and then looked for facts.

Even after years of studying human behavior, I still sometimes find myself making the same mistakes I warn other people about.

In a recent development, while working as a journalist on a murder investigation in Arkansas, I became attracted to someone I was interviewing, someone who had been good friends with a possible person of interest. I knew perfectly well that personal chemistry could interfere with my judgment but found myself getting involved anyway.

Investigative work can teach you to be skeptical, but skepticism isn't a force field. You can know that someone is wrong for you and still want them. And you can be exceptionally good at uncovering other people's secrets while remaining spectacularly talented at hiding things from yourself.

A lot of people expect me to turn into Nancy Drew with every man I meet. There’s some truth to that; like most women, I do a Google deep dive before meeting someone for the first time.

But after spending years investigating cheating spouses, con artists, and eventually a cold-case murder, I've become convinced that there's a fine line between healthy curiosity and turning your love life into a full-time surveillance operation.

I don't think women should spend their evenings running background checks on every man who buys them a cocktail. Nor should they secretly follow their partners or interpret every unanswered text as evidence of a double life.

It has been revealed that I never invade any significant others’ privacy and never would. If I don’t trust them, the relationship isn’t worth it to me. Because tracking people, online or otherwise, is exhausting. And I already have enough of that in my day job!

Industry observers note that for years, I thought being a good investigator meant finding answers to every question. Now I think one of the most notable skills—both in detective work and in dating—is knowing when you have enough information to make a decision. And when it's time to stop investigating and get on with your life.

Catherine Townsend is an investigative journalist, licensed private investigator, and host of the true-crime podcast Hell and Gone. Her new book, HOW TO SURVIVE A MURDER INVESTIGATION: A True Story of Death and Danger in the Ozarks, is out now.

Everything Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams Have Said About Their Friendship

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Storrie and Williams have been open in interviews about their experience creating the show, along with their offscreen relationship as they navigate sudden fame together.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

HBO Max and Crave’s Heated Rivalry has quickly become one of the most-discussed series of the year, catapulting its stars Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams into the celebrity stratosphere. The two actors portray hockey players Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie), who have a secret love affair spanning almost a decade. The series is known for its spicy intimate scenes as well as its beautiful depiction of romantic yearning.

Storrie and Williams have been open in interviews about their experience creating the show, along with their offscreen relationship as they navigate sudden fame together.

“Hudson is my best friend, and I literally can’t fathom doing this without him,” Storrie told W magazine in December 2025. “We were both in similar places in life before this. We quit our jobs within a day of each other. We booked this and flew out the same day. Now it’s turning into two people who are being seen internationally for the first time. This has been the highlight of my life, and meeting Hudson makes that 10 times sweeter.”.

Here, everything the two actors have shared about their friendship.

Fans of the show tend to “ship” Williams and Storrie, hoping they end up dating in real life. Storrie addressed this head-on in an interview with Vulture, saying things are strictly platonic.

Sources indicate that when asked about the intimate scenes they shot in the show, Storrie said, “For me, it doesn’t feel spicy at all—like, that’s me and my best friend. This is the first time in my life I’m having this many eyes on me. They’ve seen me naked, they’ve seen me kiss, they’ve seen me be in love with a man on-screen—it’s only normal for people to try to transfer that over to mine and Hudson’s real life.” He explained that he intends to keep his private life private, adding, “I feel honored to be able to bring someone to life that so many people feel seen, understood, and represented by, and I think that transcends whoever I’m sleeping with in my real life.”.

Williams expressed a similar sentiment to Deadline, saying, “I want queer people telling queer stories, but also, there’s the element of Connor and I—we’re best friends, and we love expressing that physically. You see people who infer or assume, and you kind of have to let that go. But then again, I never wanna stop expressing the love I have for Connor physically, and I’m never really going to, and I think multiple things can be true at once.”.

In November 2026, Williams’s interview on The Assembly aired. One of the audience members there asked Williams if he ever had romantic feelings for Storrie. “No,” he replied. “Swiftly, me and Connor realized we were, like, platonic soulmates, just completely in love with each other. I think that’s what made our friendship so stable and beautiful, is that we realized we could be completely ourselves, be completely guard down. So, I think the thing that made our relationship as rich as it was is, like, me and that man could cuddle for 10 hours, and it just mean cuddling, just mean we just love each other dearly, but don’t wanna beep each other’s bop.”.

In a recent development, he then added playfully, “Who doesn’t want Connor Storrie in their shower? You know, someone needs to get my back. I wish Connor was just with me every day. I’m like, ‘Hey, I have a loofah but I can’t reach [my back].’ If I had Connor with me every day, he could just come in there.”.

Recent findings suggest that sophie Nélisse, who plays Heated Rivalry’s Rose Landry, interviewed Williams for Wonderland magazine in January 2026 and asked him how he and Storrie balance promoting the show with forging their own identities. Williams admitted that they purposely go to different events, in part to keep their friendship more private and their brands separate.

“It’s been really nice, because Connor and I are aligned,” Williams began. “We want to be different artists. We don’t want to be the Olsen twins. We want to be Connor and Hudson, with different filmographies and different deals. As much as we love each other, our friendship doesn’t need to be public. Jacob [Tierney] has that quote: ‘Shane and Ilya are for the public. Connor and Hudson are for themselves.’ And that’s how we feel. People want to see us front row together all the time, but we actively avoid that, because it starts to feel like branding. If you’re always seen together, you become attached at the hip. I FaceTime him whenever I’m free. But if we’re offered the same fashion indicates, we’re like, ‘Which one are you going to? Okay, I’ll go to a different one.’ We’re stubborn, selfish artists who want to be our own people. We’re like, ‘I love you. I don’t want to do everything with you.’”.

In a recent development, both Williams and Storrie got into great shape for the show. In a profile with GQ in December 2025, Williams talked about meeting his co-star and being intimidated by his build.

“Connor pushed himself up onto the island in the kitchen,” Williams noted. “I remember seeing his arms. They were the size of my legs. I was like, Holy fuck.”.

Sources indicate that “It’s not true,” Storrie responded. “Because you have crazy legs.”.

According to recent reports, the show’s creator, Jacob Tierney, also commented on their affection for one another in the piece, saying, “They’re living through a thing right now that is bananas—absolutely fucking bananas—and they’re handling it with grace, with humor, with generosity. They adore each other, which is like, thank fucking God.”.

While discussing his own workout routine with Men’s Health in January, Williams had a playful quip about Storrie’s physique: “I’m okay talking about my butt, but poor Connor Storrie—who has the fattest butt I’ve ever seen on a man—I’m sure just wants to stop talking about his beautiful cheeks.”.

In a December interview with Entertainment Weekly, the friends discussed a viral video from the Heated Rivalry wrap party where they are rolling around on the floor together.

“Very plainly spoken, me and Hudson are freaks,” Storrie explained. “We’re clowns. We just love to riff and have fun and go crazy, and those were two situations where we were caught off guard doing our thing. The wrap party, that was all improvised. I think we were just putting on a show.”.

Williams added, “Also, there might be something else, I think, with—we’re both very physical actors, and movement is a huge part of it.”.

During his Vulture interview, Storrie spoke about moving into an apartment next to Williams’s while filming in Toronto.

“We would literally just go to set, go home, cook, work out together, and geek out over how excited we were to finally be working on this level,” he mentioned. “If we were any less close, we probably would’ve gotten annoyed with each other really quick.”.

According to recent reports, the American actor told Vulture that they leaned into their chemistry while promoting Heated Rivalry’s first season. “If Hudson says something jokingly, like, ‘Spit in my mouth,’ I think that gives everyone else the go-ahead to get in on that too,” he said. “People are ruthless talking about our holes and our butts.”.

During his discussion with Interview, Storrie added that spending time with Williams has helped ground them both during their press tour. “Hudson’s been in town, so we’ll have some quality time and come back down to ground zero,” he mentioned. “It’s funny, because all the press and stuff is getting easier and easier and easier. You would think you would get burnt out and exhausted. Even though it’s only been three weeks of doing press for this, I’m clicking into an interesting sort of confidence and appreciation for all of this.”.

Williams, meanwhile, credited Storrie for helping him keep the press tour fun during an interview with The Hollywood Reporter. “I have one of my best friends for life right beside me through it all, which is already a luxury that a lot of actors don’t get,” he stated. “I’m sure I would’ve probably had a smaller appetite for the amount of stuff we’re doing if I didn’t have him through this. I’m an omnivert, leaning more to an extrovert, but I still get—I have ADHD, I’m unmedicated, currently, for the last while, so my social battery can just tap [out] pretty quick. At the end of the day, I’m pretty forgiving with myself if I’m talking with a reporter in a polite, more boring way. Then when I’ve had coffee, and I’ve had a nap, I let myself be chaotic. I let myself off the leash. I try to say, whatever mood I’m in, just be Canadian, don’t be mean. Whatever they get, they get.”.

Industry observers note that timid magazine asked Williams how Storrie’s acting has helped him be a better performer. Williams responded, “He’s so incredibly present and so incredibly truthful. As an actor, it’s so much easier to think of what you should be doing or what you think would be an entertaining version of this or the most dramatic version or make sure you’re hitting these lines properly or doing the scene properly or the director wants this and the script says this. But just to actually listen to the person and let what they’re saying affect you—Connor is so good at that. There’s so many moments where I am saying something and the script says he does this, and he does something so unexpectedly emotional or so unexpectedly vulnerable that even if I’m very robotic and going through a scene, he can crack me and change my trajectory in the scene. He’s a huge resource in affecting me and that makes my job way easier because I don’t have to. He makes me be present. He’s so good at that. That’s his superpower.”.

Storrie, meanwhile, credited Williams for helping him understand Ilya so swiftly in his Interview story. “I feel like I got the character pretty instantly,” he began. “I believed in his circumstances without almost any effort, and I just trusted Hudson so much. It’s so easy to act when you know where you’re coming from and you believe the person opposite you. I mean, I’m so gooey. I’m such a romantic. So any of the really heightened emotional moments—their love or confession or an outbreak or a fight—those are the moments that I really enjoy as an actor.”.

Williams listed out all the nicknames he and Storrie have for each other during his Timid magazine interview. “He calls me Huddy, Papi, Bubba, Baby,” he noted. “I call him Pookie. I used to call him Pookie a lot. Papi. Oh, Con Con. I call him that both in text form and verbally. But yeah, a lot of nicknames.”.

GQ revealed that when the series wrapped, they got matching tattoos that read “SEX SELLS.”.

The Canadian star revealed that he stayed at Storrie’s Los Angeles apartment when he came to the U.S. to do some press. “We were like, ‘Oh, my God, if people saw us just getting ready in the morning, giving each other big spooning hugs, just to say we’re proud of each other,’ people would be going crazy,” he told Variety. “If only one fan had access, God forbid. But yeah, we just love each other very dearly.”.

The outlet asked him what creating Heated Rivalry taught him. Williams responded, “I think I had my own biases, maybe that would be too strong of a word, but my own discomfort if I expressed myself fully, physically and affectionately, both with women and men. It would feel inappropriate. I realized if you really do love someone—platonically or not—I’m such a tactile, sensory person. There are so many taboos. It’s much harder on men. I had to let that go, and I got to learn how freeing that is. That also went hand-in-hand with being myself, truly as an artist. Connor was also a great person to have at my side. I think we both opened each other up to just be freer, more fully expressive.”.

Recent findings suggest that during Williams’s January 2026 appearance on Andy Cohen Live, he revealed that Storrie is an “awful texter,” but they largely keep in touch with frequent video calls. “We’ll Facetime each other or call each other randomly, very consistently,” he told the host. “That has sort of been my stability, especially through this. Just having my best friend who is in the same position I am.”.

In a November 2025 interview with The Permanent Rain Press, Williams mentioned he would pitch Storrie as “a beautiful little, sensitive little radical, artist boy. Who should be treated with the utmost care and hugs and friendliness because he can’t handle anything else. And that’s perfect. And that’s the way he should be treated.”.

He added, “And anyone who doesn’t treat him that way should die.”.

Recent findings suggest that in May 2026, Williams and Storrie made their Met Gala debut. They took a bathroom selfie together, which Williams later posted to his Threads account.

The pair’s appearance at the Met Gala excited fans, with one user taking a solo shot of Williams and posting it alongside lyrics from Rihanna’s breakup song, “Woo.” (Williams has a longtime girlfriend, Katelyn Larson.) The post has since been taken down, but Williams responded and wrote, “Rpfing [real person fan fiction] gotta stop y’all.”.

During his November interview on Vogue’s The Run-Through podcast, Storrie revealed that he and Williams were living together while shooting season 2 of Heated Rivalry.

“Right now we’re filming [the next season of Heated Rivalry], so I literally live with him, which is amazing,” he remarked. “We were at this hotel, which was a brilliant hotel, but I just….I needed a washing machine. I needed a kitchen.”.

Storrie also discussed how their red carpet looks sometimes seem coordinated without any advance planning, pointing to their similar outfits at the Vanity Fair Oscar Party.

Sources indicate that “We’ve had a few moments where it just matched. But that’s just very telling of Hudson and I in general. We are very cut from the same cloth. We have a soul tie thing. So there’s a lot of synchronicity. But no, we don’t coordinate before at all,” he noted.

He also expressed admiration for Williams’s personal style, particularly his approach to streetwear and tailoring.

“Hudson is really cool. You know what I mean? Hudson has this sort of, there’s something kind of like street style or edgy about what he does,” Storrie explained. “And like when he dresses up, when he does like fine suits and tailoring, it’s a little bit different. And I always kind of envy that, like him being able to wear really cool stuff, because it doesn’t really work the same on me. But I like my thing too.”.

A Rare Alexander McQueen Gem Is Coming to Auction

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Few remnants of fashion history manage to stir up emotions and draw headlines quite like pieces from Alexander McQueen’s revered runways.
  • Sources indicate that “Based on what we know about McQueen’s distribution at the time and the types of garments that went into production after a runway show, we estimate there were probably only fewer than two dozen examples of this exact dress produced,” Max Brownawell, head of handbags at Christie’s, tells ELLE.
  • The dress was the fourth look in the runway collection, styled with the iconic Armadillo boots.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few remnants of fashion history manage to stir up emotions and draw headlines quite like pieces from Alexander McQueen’s revered runways. Rare, technical, and sensorial, these are certainly not your average, everyday pieces of clothing. McQueen runway pieces are often flexed at the world’s top fashion exhibitions at museums around the world. That’s just one of the reasons why the multicolor silk minidress from Alexander McQueen spring/summer 2010 “Plato’s Atlantis” is the star of Christie’s December Luxury Week, where the runway gem will be hitting the auction block with a $150,000 to $300,000 estimate. The sale runs online from November 25 to December 10, 2026.

Sources indicate that “Based on what we know about McQueen’s distribution at the time and the types of garments that went into production after a runway show, we estimate there were probably only fewer than two dozen examples of this exact dress produced,” Max Brownawell, head of handbags at Christie’s, tells ELLE. “Then on top of that, the importance of ‘Plato’s Atlantis,’ as McQueen’s final fully realized collection, really can’t be understated. He himself mentioned that his previous collection was his final as a young man. And so this was his most mature, fully fledged collection that he’d ever produced.”.

The dress was the fourth look in the runway collection, styled with the iconic Armadillo boots. Designed with a futuristic sculpted drape, covered in prints from the natural world (think: a collage of abstracted imagery pulled from butterfly wings, snakeskin, and insects), the silhouette is a favorite of fashion fans and archivists. Brownawell shares that the piece still has the tag attached and has likely never been worn. The ensemble may very well exceed the estimate: for reference, a “Plato’s Atlantis” look complete with those aforementioned boots sold for $1.5 million including fees at a Fair Warning auction in Upcoming York on Sept. 17, 2026, setting an auction record for McQueen.

“He was going for something that was entirely new,” claims Brownawell. “This dress is a really prime example of that, the way that the print has been designed to lay perfectly within the architecture of the garment itself is really a spectacular sort of couture level of creation. On top of that, you have this unbelievably architectural draping, which, you know, McQueen has, it’s been mentioned that he really actually draped a lot of these pieces directly onto the forms themselves because it was so complex.”.

Aside from the dress itself, Alexander McQueen’s spring/summer 2010 show was ahead of its time in every way. It was the first show to be livestreamed in real time on the internet, and it was the first fashion show to debut a major pop single during a show; Lady Gaga’s “Bad Romance” premiered during the show’s finale. “McQueen’s legacy has been just growing stronger and stronger every year,” adds Brownawell.

It has been revealed that the dress is hitting the auction block at a time when Christie’s is launching its inaugural fashion auction. “We really believe that the market is at a point right now where people do appreciate the crucial designs,” he notes. “There’s a lot of clothing out there, but there’s also a lot of very important pieces that define what we wear and where fashion is going and where it’s been.”.

In a recent development, if you’re looking hard enough for sales on menswear, you can almost always find a discount on something decent, a pair of shoes, a shirt maybe, but you have to scrounge. Every other week of the year, that’s just how it is. But this week, the week of Black Friday, the opposite is true. Every store and their mother is having a sale and suddenly, it’s not easy to tell which markdowns are gonna go fast and which ones will still be there when you log on again in December. Luckily, you have me. Year-round, it’s my job to keep tabs on deals so I know which ones to pounce on this Black Friday.

Industry observers note that on Amazon, there’s my favorite Lacoste polo, which is actually on an outrageous sale going up to 40 percent off if you’re the right size. Filson jackets are 25 percent off. Lululemon isn’t just for the gals, it has a ton of great stuff for men and its Black Friday sale is absolutely stacked. And REI is doing its classic “We hate Black Friday but are doing a sale anyway” thing, and as always we are here for it.

It has been revealed that let’s start with the personal favorites; after that we’ll just list deals alphabetically by brand. First, Amazon. Yeah, yeah, everything is Amazon now. But when Bezos is offering big discounts on Lacoste polos and Levi’s, we listen.

It has been revealed that nothing is ever going to beat the cool of a beat-to-hell Filson jacket. If you’ve been holding off on buying one, I can’t recommend it enough. Plus, Black Friday is the perfect time to get one for 25 percent off.

FIlson Tin Cloth Insulated Jacket.

I tell regular—meaning normal guys, not fashion-y dorks like me—that Huckberry is really the answer to 90 percent of what they want. All of a man’s casual wardrobe can be bought here; the only thing it doesn’t stock well is suits and tailoring. I’m seeing up to 40 percent off on seasonal shirts, and up to 30 percent off jackets, sweaters, and pants; that’s as good as it gets, folks.

Dressing for date night is pretty simple during the spring and summer: grab a slinky tank top, slip on a mini skirt, and throw on a pair of heeled flip-flops. But once the weather cools, things get a bit trickier.

Recent findings suggest that oversized fisherman sweaters, corduroy pants, and snuggly slipper-like boots are all great for cozy, laid-back days. But sometimes you want to look a bit more elevated, whether you're heading out on a hot date or meeting your best friends for dinner. You want an outfit that feels special and isn't going to leave you shivering in the frigid cold—and Hollywood's biggest stars have it figured out.

It has been revealed that lola Tung, Kristen Bell, and Olivia Munn are a few recent celebrities spotted in cold-weather pieces, including funnel-neck band jackets, slick pants, and turtleneck dresses. Each celebrity-approved ensemble additionally includes rich winter fabrics, like suede, velvet, and leather, creating both a bold and warm fashion option.

If your calendar is stacked with dinner reservations and holiday plans, you're going to want to keep reading to discover a slew of style-forward early winter outfits, straight from your favorite celebrities to your closet.

Lola Tung knows the power of an all-black ensemble. To keep the ensemble from looking flat, she slipped on pieces featuring different finishes, like shiny leather and sheer nylon, to add dimension. This combination made each item—from her knee-high boots to her edgy band jacket—stand out. For added visual interest, Tung threw on a patchwork Coach bag in warm fall hues.

Free People Ryland Vegan Leather Band Jacket.

Reformation Carla Low-Waist Skirt.

Commando Soft Luxe Sheer Tights.

Follow Coco Rocha’s lead on the nights you’re eager to wear pants but aren’t feeling casual denim. Her rich leather trousers elevate the twisted, off-the-shoulder long-sleeve, making the outfit look thoughtfully curated (while remaining secretly comfortable). The monochromatic pieces, including Rocha’s snip-toe boots and suede coat, offer a streamlined finish.

Frame The Modernist Leather Slim-Fit Palazzo Pants.

Nordstrom Cubic Zirconia Stud Earrings.

Whether you’re hitting up your favorite dance bar or going to a swanky cocktail lounge, Meghann Fahy’s sophisticated going-out look fits the bill. While her mini dress makes for a leggy moment, the turtleneck adds warmth, with the leather bomber jacket serving as an extra layer of coziness. Pointed-toe heels are a dressy finishing touch, but you could easily swap for boots instead.

Anine Bing Leather Leon Bomber Jacket.

Zara Metallic Buckle Slingbacks.

Urban Outfitters Kayla Oval Sunglasses.

For those ultra-luxe evenings, reach for a plush velvet coat like Olivia Munn. The lustrous fabric looks elevated and expensive, doing the heavy lifting for you. Simply throw on trousers and patent leather heels to complete the look. It’s an ideal option for glamorous dinners and upcoming holiday gatherings.

DARING DIVA Velvet Lapel Double-Breasted Long Outerwear Winter Coat.

#192153. 12 Things You Should Toss From Your Kitchen ASAP Before Thanksgiving
