General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

12 Things You Should Toss From Your Kitchen ASAP Before Thanksgiving

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (816 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’ll soon be the most key day of the year in the kitchen, so give yourself the gift of space and freedom from clutter by doing a quick purge.
  • “Thanksgiving needs every inch of counter, fridge, and cabinet space you’ve got,” notes Ann Lightfoot, cofounder of DDH Home Organizing & Move Management.
  • Sources indicate that but don’t overdo it!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’ll soon be the most key day of the year in the kitchen, so give yourself the gift of space and freedom from clutter by doing a quick purge.

“Thanksgiving needs every inch of counter, fridge, and cabinet space you’ve got,” notes Ann Lightfoot, cofounder of DDH Home Organizing & Move Management. “A short edit beforehand means you can find the baster when you need it, the leftovers have somewhere to go, and you aren’t digging past three broken whisks to reach a serving spoon.”.

Sources indicate that but don’t overdo it! “You don’t need a Pinterest-perfect pantry. You need room to work,” notes Lightfoot. “A full organizing project can easily turn into a weekend of half-finished bins, and that’s the last thing anyone needs in November.”.

Instead of tearing apart the entire kitchen, focus on the areas and items that will have the most impact. “We always say edit before you organize, and this is the editing part: take things out,” claims Lightfoot. “Do one quick pass, ask whether each item earns its space, and let the rest go. Labels and matching containers can wait until January.”.

Ahead, here’s what experts say to get rid of ASAP so your kitchen will be ready for cooking and entertaining at Thanksgiving.

“Spices lose their flavor over time, and stale cinnamon or a two-year-old jar of sage will make itself known in your pie and stuffing,” states Lightfoot. “Check the dates on baking soda, baking powder, and flour too. Toss what’s past its prime and make a shopping list while you’re at it.”.

According to recent reports, glasses with scratches just don’t look great. “I'm all for mixing vintage and contemporary pieces, but damaged drinking glasses and dishes should go,” indicates Kerrie Kelly, NKBA, FASID, CEO and creative director of Kerrie Kelly Studio, and NKBA 2026 National Board Chair. “Holiday entertaining is a wonderful excuse to take inventory and make sure you have enough functional pieces for your guests.”.

“Three napkins and a stack of faded plates won't set a beautiful table. Let them go and start fresh,” indicates Nikki Boyd, organizing expert, author of Beautifully Organized, and founder of At Home With Nikki.

It’s amazing how stuff gets pushed to the back of the fridge, never to be seen again. “Fridge space is prime real estate on Thanksgiving, between the turkey, the sides, and everything guests bring,” notes Lightfoot. “Clear out the half-empty dressings, the jam from last summer, and anything you can’t identify.”.

Recent findings suggest that be honest with yourself. “If it hasn't come out for a single holiday in years, it's not waiting for this one,” says Boyd. “Keep heirlooms with stories, and release the rest.”.

According to recent reports, “Kitchen drawers have a way of collecting multiples of things we rarely need more than one of,” indicates Laura Kinsella, founder of Urban OrgaNYze. “Pull out your spatulas, peelers, measuring cups, and all those cooking tools that always seem to get stuck in the drawer. If you're not reaching for them when you're hosting 20 people, chances are you don't need them for a regular weeknight dinner either.”.

“Your table is your stage. Burnt down candles and stained runners don't belong on it,” indicates Boyd.

It has been revealed that containers that have no lids need to go away ASAP. Ditto for lids that don’t have a container. “Before the holiday leftovers start piling up, take 10 minutes to match your food storage containers with their lids. Get rid of anything that's cracked, warped, or missing its match,” indicates Kinsella. “There's nothing more frustrating than having a refrigerator full of leftovers and realizing you can't find a single lid that fits!”.

In a recent development, that bread maker you haven’t touched lately? The air fryer that’s collecting dust? It’s time to donate them. “Any significant kitchenware item that you haven’t used for the past two to three holiday seasons needs to go,” says Amelia Meena, owner of Appleshine, Organization + Design.

If they’re in bad shape, treat yourself to some newly introduced ones. “Nonstick pans with a flaking coating and sheet pans warped beyond saving make cooking harder than it has to be,” says Lightfoot. “If you’ve been meaning to replace one, do it now so you aren’t stuck mid-recipe.”.

Industry observers note that soy sauce and ketchup packets, plastic forks, extra napkins, and the stack of menus add up rapidly. You’ll want that drawer space for foil, twine, and the meat thermometer, so toss the whole lot into the garbage immediately, notes Lightfoot.

Stained, threadbare towels and thin pot holders aren’t safe for pulling a hot roasting pan out of the oven—plus, raggedy mitts don’t exactly scream “festive.” Pitch thin pot holders and recycle old towels into cleaning rags, then treat yourself to a cute new set of kitchen linens, notes Lightfoot.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you have a keen eye for a fashionable investment—whether it’s a vintage accessory, a high-quality classic, or a trendy piece to keep your wardrobe current. But your closet isn’t the only arena that’s kept up to date. With your finger on the pulse of all things elegant and practical, no doubt the latest and greatest in personal transportation—electric cars—is firmly on your radar. This automotive upgrade is a step toward the future, and, like all new things, comes with some specific guidelines. With the help of State Farm, we’ve outlined what to consider before you elevate your status to EV owner—from how the flexibility of an EV factors into your routine, travel aims, and commute to how best to protect your fabulous new asset.

Industry observers note that when choosing an EV, consider how it fits into your lifestyle. Location, budget, and driving habits should all play a role in finding the right fit. For example, if you spend a lot of time on the highway, a hybrid may make more sense than an all-electric model since you’ll have gas as a backup when your battery runs low. You’ll also want to think about how much passenger and cargo space you need—if you’re regularly hauling people, pets, or plenty of (literal) baggage, compare the costs of larger models that can accommodate everything comfortably.

Recent findings suggest that you love vintage, but does that extend to your car? It just depends on your needs.

Sources indicate that when deciding to buy pre-owned or newly introduced, think about how long you’re looking to own the car. Consider battery wear and how much it costs to replace one, your total budget (including financing, maintenance, and insurance), and whether or not you’re eligible for any tax credits that could offset the price of a new EV.

Yes, you’re already envisioning yourself pulling onto the street in your fabulous newly introduced ride, but make sure you weigh the pros and cons to save yourself from buyer’s remorse later.

Recent findings suggest that you passionately curate your life, and the same should go for your electric car’s coverage. When considering insurance, EVs require a bit of what non-electric cars need, along with a few additional protections.

According to recent reports, protecting yourself and your investment starts with liability, collision, and comprehensive, just like with traditional cars. But with an EV, you’ll also need to cover battery damage, charging equipment, and specialized repairs. As a result—and because of higher purchase prices, specialized parts and repairs, and more—pricing tends to be higher than on policies for traditional cars. Manage these costs by comparing quotes on the model you choose, taking advantage of discounts for anti-theft devices and safe driving records, and, if you can help manage the potential out-of-pocket cost, adjusting your deductible a bit higher to lower your monthly payments.

In a recent development, you don’t need to do this all alone, though. Just like you’d turn to a trusted friend for a second opinion on your outfit, State Farm is there to answer your EV insurance questions and offer you an insurance quote before you buy.

When shopping for an EV, think about how far you’ll typically drive, where you’ll charge, and how long charging will take. Most EVs can go around 200 miles on a full charge at lower city speeds, but your charging setup matters, too. If you’re planning to charge at home, you’ll want to factor in installation of a charger, electricity costs, and potential homeowners insurance considerations. If you’ll rely on public chargers, make sure there’s a reliable network along your usual routes. It’s also worth knowing what kind of charger your car uses: Level 1 chargers plug into a standard outlet and can take up to 24 hours, while Level 2 chargers use a 240-volt outlet and offer a faster, more convenient option for home charging.

Much like you carry a purse-sized mending kit for fashion fixes, it’s always good to have an EV backup plan for automotive emergencies.

Add EV-specific roadside assistance to your insurance blueprint.

Collision or comprehensive insurance could cover this, or your warranty may cover normal degradation.

After your deductible payment, collision or comprehensive coverage should help lower costs.

The answer varies by model, so do your research, but know that you can add gap insurance or fresh car replacement to your blueprint to mitigate the glitch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

It has been revealed that the most wonderful time of the year is one filled with traditions and rituals. It’s also a time of whimsy and a whole lot of sparkle. This season, consider enhancing some of your favorite holiday scenes with items that are fun, festive, and decidedly on trend. Whether you’re into retro pieces collected over the years, traditional plaids and patterns, or natural greenery, you’re likely to find a theme that fits with your personal style and how your family celebrates. “Your home shouldn’t suddenly become an entirely different house because it’s Christmas. It should still feel like you,” claims Jade Joyner, Founder and Principal designer of Metal + Petal in Georgia.

In a recent development, with that in mind, Lowe’s carries everything you need to incorporate these trends into your holiday decorating: from classic lights and trees to quirky ornaments and outdoor decor. Below, we’ve defined the holiday decor trends by designers for 2026, and included the Lowe’s items that can help you pull off the look at home.

2026 Holiday Decor Trends at a Glance.

Collected Nostalgia: Embrace kitsch and joy with vintage-inspired blow molds, animatronics, and retro multi-colored lights.

Rich, Moody Colors: Move beyond the all-white Christmas with color-drenched spaces featuring deep burgundy, emerald green, and brown accents.

Joyful Tones: Refresh traditional palettes with unexpected, playful pops of pink, pale blue, and lime green.

Natural Textures: Ground your space with foraged greenery, fresh cedar garlands, dried oranges, and handwoven rattan.

Americana Christmas: Layer plaids, velvet, and antique-inspired brass for a soft, handed-down aesthetic that feels deeply personal.

Recent findings suggest that this year, people are embracing holiday styles that bring them joy, rather than those that just look good on social media—and nostalgic pieces often do just that. From vintage-inspired blow molds that feature beloved ‘80s and ‘90s icons, to trees pre-lit with large, multi-colored lights, this style is all about adding in a bit of your childhood Christmas into your adult home. “This nostalgia trend isn’t precious or perfect. It’s mix-and-match with a lot of kitsch,” explains Janette Ewen, Designer and Creative Director of Parker Barrow Design in Los Angeles, who has styled hotels, inns, and magazine photo shoots for the holiday season. Beyond blow molds and multi-colored lights, animatronic characters from classic stop-motion Christmas films can add a vintage touch to your outdoor decor.

Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer Outdoor Christmas Decoration.

Peanuts 24-in LED Snoopy Christmas Blow Mold.

Holiday Living 7.5-ft Vintage Pine Pre-lit Artificial Christmas Tree.

Just as more people are incorporating color into their interior design, expect to see more colorful holiday decor this year. Think rich palettes of deep red, burgundy, emerald greens, and even dark brown. “Color in general is making a comeback and all-white Christmas seems to be taking a backseat,” explains Sarah Fontanez, Founder of Florida-based interior design firm Pomme House. Color-drenching (decorating in all one color) is expected to be popular, especially among those who like an avant-garde, creative look, notes Ewen. If you’re not ready to commit to a single tone, adding just a few velvet-flocked emerald ornaments, deep red satin bows, or even brown or purple stockings can deepen the color wheel.

Holiday Living 8-pack Flocked Dark Green Ball Christmas Ornament Set.

6-Pack 18-in Christmas Stocking.

Holiday Living 4-pack Satin Red Bow Christmas Ornament Set.

Adding in unexpected colors, like pinks, blues, or even lime green, to the traditional Christmas palette of red and green can help your decor feel fresh. “Red and pink together absolutely spark joy for me. I love the playfulness of it, especially mixed with traditional greenery, beautiful ribbons, and vintage ornaments,” Joyner explains. Expect to see pale blue added to the mix as well—many designers pair it with deep brown or burgundy. A few ornaments in one of these colors can give your tree a whole upcoming feel. Of course, a few strands of twinkling, multi-colored lights can also bring a playful touch to your decor.

Garvee 12-pack Shatterproof Velvet Christmas Ornaments.

Holiday Living 100-count 24.77-ft Twinkling LED String Lights |.

Bringing a bit of the outdoors in through cedar garlands, rattan baskets, and pine cones is a seasonal look that will look just as fitting in late winter as it did when paired with your red and green holiday decor. “I think inviting the outdoors inside with natural greenery feels grounding and warm,” explains Iowa-based designer Brooke Mennen-Talsma. “Fresh cedar, pine, and foraged branches make a home feel collected and nothing beats the smell of walking in the door.” Weaving foraged items like pine cones, willow branches, or birch pieces into artificial cedar wreaths or garlands will ensure your greenery stays, well, green all season long. A hand-woven rattan tree skirt can complement these elements, while a string of dried oranges can add a hint of color that still feels natural.

Etokfoks 28-in Wicker Christmas Tree Collar Handwoven Rattan.

Holiday Living 24-in Indoor/Outdoor Artificial Real Feel Cedar Wreath.

Holiday Living Holiday Living 6-ft Indoor/Outdoor Artificial Real Feel Cedar Christmas Garland.

ZHANYIGY Natural Dried Orange Slices Cinnamon Sticks and Pinecones.

It has been revealed that antique-inspired Christmas decor that looks like it’s been in the family for generations can feel soft and homey at the holidays, especially when paired with traditional elements. “We’re seeing a return to plaids, velvet, vintage-inspired ornaments, paper chains, and classic holiday colors,” Joyner notes. Brass bells, taper candles, and oversized bows can also make decor look handed-down and collected, she adds. Of course, starting your own tradition (like handmaking a paper chain or giving your children a new ornament every year) can make this trend feel more intentional—making it one you’ll look forward to for years to come.

Greendale Home Fashions Plaid Fabric Christmas Pillow.

ZHLKING 4-Pack Tartan Plaid Stockings Holiday Decor.

Holiday Living 48-pack Candy Cane Shatterproof Christmas Ornament Set.

Aoile Set of 5 Gold Metal Christmas Bell Hanging Ornaments.

What are the biggest holiday decorating trends this year?Nostalgic holiday looks inspired by your childhood favorites, along with antique traditional elements, colorful decorations, and natural greenery are all having a moment this season.

What Christmas colors are trending this season?Deep, rich hues like burgundy, evergreen, dark brown, and deep blue are set to replace the pared-back, all-white Christmas look. Touches of pink, pale blue, and even lime green can make these luxe colors feel a bit more relaxed. What trending holiday decorations can I shop for at Lowe’s?Lowe’s has plenty of nostalgic outdoor decor, like blow molds and animatronics, right alongside luxe cedar garlands, velvet-flocked holiday ornaments, and vintage-inspired elements like oversize bows and faux brass candlesticks.

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1488 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: 9 Interior Trends Designers Are Officially Ditching in 2027

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1488 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The end of the year is a great time to look back and reflect.
  • We love predicting what’s going to be hot in home design for the upcoming seasons; however, you can’t talk about what’s going to be “in” without also touching on what’s going to be “out.” We asked a handful of designers to share what design choices and interior trends they saw a lot of in 2026 that they’re more than happy to leave behind in 2027.
  • We spend so much time making our interiors warm and reflective of our personalities, it would be a shame to ruin the look of these spaces by opting for one-dimensional lighting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The end of the year is a great time to look back and reflect. When it comes to home design, there’s a lot to cover, from new trends to furniture collaboration drops to specific internet-breaking interiors. One of our favorite things to do around this time is figure out what’s coming next in terms of interiors.

We love predicting what’s going to be hot in home design for the upcoming seasons; however, you can’t talk about what’s going to be “in” without also touching on what’s going to be “out.” We asked a handful of designers to share what design choices and interior trends they saw a lot of in 2026 that they’re more than happy to leave behind in 2027. Keep reading to find out the nine things they said.

We spend so much time making our interiors warm and reflective of our personalities, it would be a shame to ruin the look of these spaces by opting for one-dimensional lighting.

It has been revealed that “It's time to move beyond relying on a single overhead fixture or wall-to-wall recessed lighting to illuminate an entire room,” designer Kristen Mendoza of Four Brothers Design + Build claims. “Flat, overly bright lighting can make even the most beautifully designed spaces feel sterile and uninviting.”.

Instead, incorporating layers of lighting to add dimension and create a warm atmosphere is much better for your home. Sconces, picture lights, table lamps, and thoughtfully placed accent lighting at various heights throughout the room, Mendoza adds, give a space a more intimate touch.

Sources indicate that “I also recommend using warm 2700K light sources on dimmers to flatter people, highlight architectural details, and bring out the natural beauty of materials,” she explains. “Lighting should be considered early in the design and construction process, not treated as an afterthought.”.

Sources indicate that part of the appeal of “grandma chic” decor is that it’s been collected over time. The pieces show their age, the interior is imperfect, and it’s very clearly reflective of the homeowner’s personality and life. However, “there is a difference between a room that feels ‘collected over time’ and one that feels inherited all at once,” designer Stephanie Kraus explains, and she’s tired of seeing this false presentation on display in people’s homes.

“Heavy Roman shades with lots of fabric, chintz on top of chintz on top of chintz, fringe on every edge, etc.,” she adds. “One of these details in a room can be charming, but if you use them all together, the room can start to feel like a period movie set.”.

It’s often clear when this eccentric aesthetic is manufactured rather than effortless. Instead of trying to make the “ideal” interior in the span of a month, be patient and work on your home over a greater span of time. That way, the end product will look authentic.

In a recent development, though curved sofas are massively popular right now and look gorgeous in a photograph, Kraus is ready to leave them in 2026. “A curved sofa rarely seats more than two people comfortably,” she states. “Once guests settle in, everyone ends up sitting awkwardly, and conversation feels harder than it should.”.

She’s all for a sofa or couch being something that invites people in to linger over conversations and stay late into the night, and a kidney-shaped seat isn’t going to do that.

It has been revealed that while designer Maggie Vollrath of Provision Studios loved seeing the return of decorative, playful details like ruffles and scalloped edges, she thinks we’ve gone a bit overboard in 2026. These touches are being applied to just about everything: upholstery, pillows, lampshades, bedding, furniture—the list could go on.

“These details can be incredibly charming, but when they're repeated throughout an entire room, they begin to lose the very character that makes them special,” she says.

Rather than treat every piece of a room with one of these details, Vollrath suggests opting for a scalloped lampshade or a beautifully tailored ruffled pillow instead to still capture that charm without drowning the space in them.

“Limiting these details to one or two thoughtful applications allows them to feel intentional rather than overly thematic,” she adds. “Sometimes, the most interesting interiors are as much about what you choose to leave out as what you include.”.

“I'd love to see us move away from selecting materials simply because they imitate the appearance of something more expensive,” Vollrath explains. This goes beyond marble-printed contact paper and burl wood veneer; the designer means on a larger scale, like mass-produced tile that’s made to replicate the imperfections of handmade zellige.

Sources indicate that “Part of what makes authentic zellige so beautiful is the craftsmanship and natural variation that comes from its production,” she indicates. “When those qualities are artificially reproduced, I think we sometimes lose the very thing that made the original material special.”.

She would rather see a greater appreciation for beautiful, honest materials at every price point, and if the exact thing a homeowner wants is out of budget, then her solution would be to pivot the idea altogether rather than find something cheaply made that looks like what they desire.

“A classic Carrara marble paired with beautifully considered cabinetry can create an incredibly sophisticated interior, even when something as dramatic as Calacatta Viola isn't within the budget,” Vollrath explains.

In a recent development, we could probably say this every year, but it bears repeating: Don’t solely follow trends! “Just because something is trending doesn't mean it's right for your home,” designer Drew Michael Scott of Lone Fox states. “Polka dots are having a moment right now, but they don't make sense in many homes, or dare I say, most homes.”.

Sources indicate that he suggests thinking of home trends as prompts that should get you to brainstorm new ideas for your space that actually fit your style. Take polka dots again. If you want to introduce a new pattern to your home, but you don’t particularly mesh with polka dots, try a stripe instead.

“If you try to force something you don't love into your home just because it's trending, you're going to drive yourself crazy,” he adds. Let’s leave this line of thinking back in 2026 once and for all.

While we love a good built-in bookshelf and wooden ceiling beam, those types of architectural details don’t always make sense in every single home. In 2026, as personality-filled interiors became more popular for everyone, a lot of homeowners looked into adding this type of millwork to their spaces as a way to add more visual interest and texture.

“Decorative beams, arches, and elaborate millwork can feel forced when they don't make sense with the architecture of the home,” designer Dani Flax of Pearson Design Group argues. “I think there's a tendency to add these elements to make a space feel more interesting, but the result can actually take away from the architecture itself.”.

A home in a modern farmhouse style, for example, would look a bit odd with an intricate ceiling medallion and excessive picture frame molding. Design your interior around the existing architecture and the style of your home, don’t incorporate these elements simply because they’re everywhere right now.

In a recent development, the next year is not about playing it safe with your interiors—designers are tired of the stark white home. While ubiquitous gray and white color schemes had their time, they can often make a home feel generic and devoid of character.

“In their place, we're embracing more intentional, tonal palettes and color drenching,” Mendoza says.

You can still have a mostly white house, of course, but take a little risk and mix in some pops of color and pattern here and there, or choose a beautiful neutral wood tone for your cabinetry instead of a bright white paint.

“Taking a considered color, whether it's a deep green, warm clay, or earthy mushroom, and carrying it across walls, trim, and cabinetry creates a cohesive, enveloping effect,” Mendoza adds. “The goal isn't necessarily to introduce more color, but to use it with greater confidence and purpose.”.

This is definitely a hot take, but designer John Maloney McNamara of Coosa Interiors is ready to leave velvet upholstery behind. “I’ve tried, but velvet almost always reads as either a 1990s prom limo or a hotel lobby trying very hard,” he explains. “The sheen indicates every crush and bruise, and it ages into something that looks tired rather than loved.”.

Industry observers note that if you love the look of velvet, he suggests going with a mohair fabric instead, saying it has all of velvet’s depth and none of its shine. It also only gets better with age. And though he knows creamy bouclé has been overdone, Maloney McNamara thinks it deserves a reprise, but only in a rich color that can replace velvet still.

Growing up in Southern California, I was a flip-flop girl through and through. But since moving to Upcoming York, I've come to appreciate the importance of a cold-weather shoe collection. In fact, boots now outnumber sandals in my closet.

Industry observers note that whether I'm wearing a plaid mini skirt and sheer tights or straight-leg denim and a knitted sweater, boots complete the look. They're what ballet flats are to the warmer seasons, providing a tried-and-true footwear staple to rely on for the rest of fall and all winter long.

Industry observers note that while I certainly own a few striking pairs of boots (like bubblegum-pink iterations and cow-print block heels), curating a timeless collection that effortlessly pairs with your wardrobe is essential. This way, you can build upon the curated collection season after season, rather than splurging on trend-specific footwear every fall. Because these styles can be worn for years to come, investing in quality pieces that will stand the test of time is key.

In a recent development, there's still a month of fall left, and these five styles will carry you through winter too. Ahead, discover the ultimate fall boots starter pack, including classic knee-highs, Western boots, and rich burgundy hues.

According to recent reports, if you only own one pair of boots, make it these. The little black dress of footwear can be dressed up or down, transcending occasion, age, and style. The sleek and timeless shoe has even elevated my simple shift dresses with ease. Suede iterations offer a cozy appeal, slick leather delivers sophistication, stilettos are sultry, and block heels are comfortable.

Sam Edelman Sylvia Knee-High Boots.

Free People Kiki Kitten-Heel Boots.

Stuart Weitzman Stuart Leather Power Boots.

On casual fall days, the '70s-style pull-on boot will be your best friend. The straight, stovepipe shaft skips zippers in favor of pull tabs. Typically hitting at the mid-calf or knee, the heritage style boasts a low, stacked heel and sturdy sole. Wear the boots with a mini skirt, tights, and a chunky button-up cardigan for a cozy, laid-back look.

Free People Blaze Pull On Boots.

Steve Madden Riggs Banana Leather Square Toe Boots.

Like black, brown, and navy, burgundy acts as a neutral come fall. The deep, saturated color feels grounded, while still bold enough to make an impact with a simple outfit. If you're looking for a style that is fashion-forward but still timeless, this is it. Rich velvets, warm suede, and textured bouclé effortlessly pair with the deep red shade.

Jeffrey Campbell Raqib Stiletto Boots.

When I don't want to tuck a tall boot beneath my pants (think flare jeans and billowy trousers), I reach for ankle boots instead. The short shaft looks clean underneath denim, silk, cotton, and wool, creating a smooth finish that never looks frumpy. A neutral beige shade ensures your short boots pair with everything from a colorful knit shrug to a cream sweater dress.

Tory Burch Asymmetric Cap Toe Ankle Boots.

It has been revealed that you don't need to be on a ranch to wear Western boots. The rodeo-inspired footwear is officially a part of the cool-girl uniform because it's both utilitarian and dressy. While it's certainly more adventurous than the other options on this list, it's just as practical, especially when you choose an earthy hue. Style your cowgirl boots with a Fair Isle pullover and billowy skirt for an of-the-moment take.

Ariat Hazen X Toe Western Boots.

Free People Brayden Western Boots.

Dingo Dingo Love Bug Western Boots.

Breaking: 6 Stylish Ways Designers Make Vintage Tile the Star of the Room

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When we redesign, remodel, and renovate, it can be tempting to revision, replace, and modernize every nook and cranny of your home.
  • Industry observers note that “I love the irregularities you find in older tiles, whether it's subtle variations in color, an imperfect glaze, or the undulation of a tile's surface.
  • “Just like in other areas of the home, introducing a vintage element helps to create more interesting, storied spaces,” states Johanna Lyle, founder of Jo Lyle & Co.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When we redesign, remodel, and renovate, it can be tempting to revision, replace, and modernize every nook and cranny of your home. But the goal is rarely to chase newness. It’s easy to see vintage details, like quirky tile, as an obstacle standing between your home and a modern look, but tearing it out might make your heart ache later.

Industry observers note that “I love the irregularities you find in older tiles, whether it's subtle variations in color, an imperfect glaze, or the undulation of a tile's surface. Those imperfections are what make them so beautiful, giving a room texture, character, and a sense of craftsmanship,” claims Ali Burgoon Nolan, founder and principal designer at Studio Burgoon. Tile is one of the vintage details homeowners regret removing the most, as modern-day designs and materials lack the panache, durability, and craftsmanship of decades past. Not to mention, the removal and reinstallation will cost you a big chunk of your budget.

“Just like in other areas of the home, introducing a vintage element helps to create more interesting, storied spaces,” states Johanna Lyle, founder of Jo Lyle & Co. “When we mix elements from different eras, the home feels more unique and collected over time. If you've bought an old home and aren't sure you love the existing, perhaps historic, tile, try to change some things around it before you give up on it completely. You might not dig it just because you haven't seen it before, or it's not what is right now popular.”.

If you’re lucky enough to have inherited vintage tile in your historic home, here are six ways designers have given it the main character energy it deserves.

Jennie Bishop preserved the charm of this century-old Illinois foyer by buffing the shine back into the home’s original tile. Her team then refinished the adjacent wood staircase and painted the walls a creamy white to brighten the room.

Designer Galena Younger knows potential when she sees it, and this historic cottage in San Antonio was no exception. The home’s original Mexican-style tiles surround the living room hearth, complemented by family heirlooms scattered around the room for an ultrapersonal, deliciously vintage aesthetic.

It has been revealed that interior and jewelry designer Trish Becker preserved this home’s original tile mantel, using it as the starting point for the room’s design. A corn-husk woven rug adds earthy warmth, while touches of green connect the room’s architectural details to its bold patterned slipper chairs.

With the goal of restoring her home’s “1931 glory,” designer Claire Thomas was ecstatic to find this bathroom’s original purple untouched, despite many renovations by previous owners. Playing on the hue, she brought in soft floral wallpaper and skirted purple stools for a feminine edge, finishing the room with a sage vanity for a pop of color and soft contrast.

Sources indicate that artist Dana Gibson and interior designer Sara Hillery brought a playful touch to this sunroom, keeping the home’s original tile floors as the foundation. They drew out the tiles’ blue tones in the plush textiles, then added woven furniture to complement its earthy browns.

Recent findings suggest that it doesn’t get more classic than a black-and-white design scheme. In this Richmond bath, Gibson and Hillery leaned into the existing retro tiles, opting to carry the palette through the room’s entire design.

The two appeared on Today three days later to address their viral fight, revealing that they’ve only been together for “two months and one week”...and most people didn’t even know they were dating until they appeared on ESPN together.

We may never know exactly what was said during that tense exchange, but there are certainly theories. The Latest York Post even tapped Nicola Hickling, in partnership with LipReader, to give her expert take on the convo. According to her, the back-and-forth involved Flournoy seemingly telling Wall, “I know he’s a piece of shit, but I value human life,” to which she seemingly agreed, “Okay. So do I.”.

Sources indicate that per Hickling, Wall possibly went on to say, “Are you suggesting I would follow you to the end of the earth? Why the fuck would I do that? Do you remember that? Are you serious right now? Do you think I expected you to do that?”.

The argument then seemingly concluded with Flournoy saying, “I am completely serious. No excuses, that’s it,” and Wall replying, “I believe you.”.

Inside Anmer Hall, Kate Middleton and Prince William’s Country Retreat

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (907 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday.
  • Local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times.
  • It has been revealed that anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday. Two masked men reportedly broke into Anmer Hall, their Georgian estate in Norfolk. Located on the grounds of the Sandringham Estate, the landmark house is where the Prince and Princess of Wales like to spend holidays and weekends with their three children, and it was also where Catherine recuperated from surgery and cancer treatments in 2024.

Local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times. The estate itself was unoccupied at the time of the break-in, according to police, and the suspects remain in custody.

It has been revealed that anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage. It’s a royal residence filled with equal parts gravitas and style. Take a closer look inside below.

Anmer Hall is in the quaint village of Anmer in Norfolk, a coastal county in northeastern England about a three-hour drive from London. The ten-bedroom Georgian pile, built in 1802, is part of Sandringham Estate, a sprawling 20,000-acre property dotted with churches, parishes, and country houses, that has been connected to the royals since 1862. The estate’s grand residence, Sandringham House, is the country bolthole of King Charles III and Queen Camilla, where royal Christmases are famously hosted. Anmer Hall is just a five-minute drive away.

According to recent reports, while you can book tours of Sandringham House and even rent properties on the greater estate, Anmer Hall is a private family residence. The village of Anmer includes a church and quaint cottages, many of which were built in the early 20th century for Edward VII, according to an architectural guide to Norfolk by Nikolaus Pevsner and Bill Wilson. The U.K.’s Office for National Statistics states that Anmer parish had a population of about 250 in 2017.

Anmer Hall was the seat of the Coldham family until Prince Albert Edward (aka the future Edward VII) purchased it in 1896 to be a part of the Sandringham Estate, Pevsner and Wilson note. The two-story house’s “charming” brick facade, made from red and brown brick, features 13 bays and dormer windows in the attic. The house underwent renovations in the years following Edward VII’s purchase.

It has been revealed that over the next century, the house was leased to numerous members of the British aristocracy, including the Duke and Duchess of Kent from 1972 to 1990, and Hugh van Cutsem, one of King Charles III’s best friends. Following the expiration of van Cutsem’s lease, the property was rented to timber manufacturer owner James Everett.

Recent findings suggest that in 2013, two years after William and Kate’s marriage, it was rumored that the royal couple would be moving in. The pair had been renting a farmhouse in Anglesey, off the northwest coast of Wales, while Prince William worked as a helicopter pilot and while they were expecting their first child, Prince George. “[Anmer Hall] would seem to be an ideal choice in that it’s close to Grandma—but not too close,” former royal correspondent Michael Cole told the BBC. Later that year, it was confirmed that William and Kate would be moving into their upcoming “baby bunker” with Prince George. But they wouldn’t physically move in until two years later, when Kate was expecting their second child, Princess Charlotte, to allow time for a $2 million refurbishment, which included a new roof, additional trees for privacy, and interior improvements.

In 2017, Meghan Markle and Prince Harry stayed with William and Kate at Anmer Hall, “because the sovereign still won’t permit unwed couples to sleep together under her roof Sandringham,” according to the book Notorious Royal Marriages by Leslie Carroll.

Today, the Prince and Princess of Wales spend most of their time at their latest primary royal residence Forest Lodge on the grounds of Windsor Castle—but they use Anmer as a country escape. The family also spent the Covid lockdown at Anmer Hall.

As part of the property’s improvements, the Prince and Princess of Wales tapped architect Charles Morris for the renovation and designer Ben Pentreath—the designer who overhauled Kate and William’s apartment at Kensington Palace, per House & Garden—for the interiors.

It has been revealed that pentreath’s firm describes its approach as one “that draws inspiration in equal measure from the great English practitioners of the 18th and 19th centuries, and from the 1960s and ’70s…but always infused with a fresh, modern sensibility”—and the same style can be seen in snippets of Anmer Hall that eagle-eyed viewers have spotted in the Prince and Princess of Wales’s social media feeds. The home—with its high ceilings and decorative moldings—is painted in soothing, neutral colors (though the dining room is reportedly a deep green hue) and accessorized with houseplants, antiques, and gilt-framed art.

Additional amenities on the property include a pool and a tennis court; Anmer Hall also hosts its own honeybee colony. And one last bonus: The home is even said to be haunted by its own ghost.

Geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Content warning: This story contains religious slurs and details about sexual and religious abuse.

Industry observers note that I was violated by a group of strangers who took turns stripping me of my hijab. It started with them exposing my hair and making hateful remarks about the hijab. Then it rapidly escalated. They removed my clothes to expose my body. They wrote degrading words on me. They encouraged each other. My protests only made them do it more.

It started out as an otherwise happy moment for me. I was attending the historic inauguration of Mayor Zohran Mamdani and celebrating the first Muslim mayor in Newly introduced York City’s history. It was an occasion being celebrated by not just New Yorkers but also fellow Americans and people around the world for the symbol of increasing visibility and inclusion that the moment represented for so many of us. I snapped a quick selfie in front of the stage with the inauguration banner billowing behind me.

Sources indicate that in the selfie, I’m bundled up in a burgundy fur-trimmed coat, my hijab clinging to my head against the cold winter wind. I’m proudly smiling at the camera. Despite the cold, I’m so happy. It was this photo, uploaded to my X account, that owners prompted Grok to regenerate in rapid succession in ways that violated my consent and religious autonomy. They used an AI chatbot to digitally take control of my body to inflict their abuse.

“I’ve always wondered what you all whackos look like without all that mess.”.

I founded Muslim Girl, a digital media platform, as a teenager to reclaim our narratives and identities online. I wanted Muslim women to speak for ourselves, on our own terms, instead of allowing others to define us. I’ve dedicated my career to empowering women to take control of their own choices. But in a matter of moments, Grok robbed me of mine.

According to recent reports, elon Musk, the owner of xAI, essentially removed all the guardrails from Grok to compete in the AI race. By allowing Grok’s image generation feature to remove clothing and promote its “spicy” capabilities, Musk was banking on users using it for sexual purposes without any regard to the harms it would cause.

The person I was most afraid to tell was my dad. After my mom passed away a few years ago, he’s become way more protective of his only daughter, and for an old-school Arab Muslim immigrant, I didn’t know how he would react. He was furious. At first, I was afraid he was going to be mad at me for being in this situation since I have always been a vocally public woman online. But he understood very rapidly that technology was being used to inflict the same abuse I had gotten used to online in more advanced and extreme ways.

Most of my elders don’t know the difference between AI-generated images and real photos, especially those who habitually forward chain messages in massive WhatsApp family group chats. My dad had to figure out a way to preemptively and sensitively explain to them what happened. Even though the images weren’t technically real, the humiliation of having to explain them to family and friends remained the same.

It has been revealed that coming from a religiously conservative background heightened the feeling of violation I experienced. The hijab is meant to be a woman’s choice. I’ve worn mine since I was 13 years old, so no public photos of me exist without me wearing it. I wear the hijab not out of heightened strictness or chastity, but rather as a guard against the male gaze in a hypersexualized society that commodifies women’s bodies and pressures us into how we should look or present ourselves.

According to recent reports, once the choice to cover or uncover is taken from a woman, it can easily become a tool of control and dominance over her body. In France, we’ve seen the proposal of a hijab ban that would fine women for covering, at the same time as we’ve watched countries like Afghanistan force women to cover. In all cases, the point is asserting power over women’s bodies.

In a recent development, technology has created new ways to violate our autonomy while our current laws struggle to keep pace with protecting our rights in the AI era. Our bodies are still a battleground. Only now, the battleground is digital.

When the notifications started pouring in, I didn’t know what to do against the faceless mob that was using Grok to replicate and violate my identity in such shocking ways. I called the police, and when they came over, I had to endure the first humiliating experience of showing them the photos. They took a police report, mentioned there was nothing they could do, and suggested that I make my account private. I refuse to diminish myself from the public at risk of having my basic rights and dignity violated online. None of us should have to.

That’s why I’m suing Elon Musk’s xAI. This isn’t just about my hijab or even about me. It’s about what we will and will not allow AI to do to us. I hope this becomes a landmark case that draws a line for the rights we are entitled to online. Even if it means standing up to the richest man on Earth.

If there's one outerwear trend I can't stop noticing this season, it's faux fur. And Kylie Jenner's fashion brand KHY has certainly caught my attention. I can’t scroll on TikTok without someone mentioning how nice Jenner’s coat selection is. And given that they’re always sold out, I wanted to see what the hype was all about. KHY debuted in 2023, and while the brand has been releasing interesting pieces, their regular clothing hasn’t always grabbed my attention. But these coats seem to be the rising notable staple fashion people are wanting to buy.

Online shopping isn’t always the easiest, especially when it comes to coats. So, for my Los Angeles fashion lovers, you can experience KHY a little more close-up in the coming weeks. KHY will be opening up the I <3 LA POP-UP, its first space of its own, on Sunset Boulevard in West Hollywood. The limited-time pop-up will be open from Friday, December 4 through Sunday, December 13, and will feature an assortment of KHY's best sellers and exclusive pieces, including the KHY After Dark coats—which are the pieces I was able to snag for this review that are right now sold out on the website.

Because there is a ton of interest, I tried two of KHY's faux-fur coats for myself, photographing each to see how they look away from the perfectly styled campaign images. From the fit and feel to the overall finish, here's my honest verdict on whether Kylie Jenner's faux-fur coats deserve a place in your winter wardrobe.

Recent findings suggest that this coat immediately caught my attention while on the KHY site. I love a dramatic moment and this fits the bill. I got the most compliments while wearing this black faux-fur coat and it makes sense because it’s the epitome of opulence. I’m wearing a 3X and I will say it’s a bit snug. I normally wear a 16/18 U.S. women’s, so that would translate to a 1X or 2X depending on the brand, so definitely sizing up would be ideal if you want a bit more room in your fit. The arm length was great and I dealt with minimal shedding.

Sources indicate that funny enough, I didn’t love this coat when I first pulled it out of the package, but my coworker and I laughed at how once I put it on it was actually so much cuter. This was also a fan favorite from one of my friends, as he said it seems “more versatile” than the dramatic all-black one. So if you’re looking for an everyday faux-fur coat, this one is definitely top of mind. This was also a 3X and it actually fit much looser than the Marmont Sculpted Coat, but the fur trim did interfere with the zipper that’s tucked beneath the chest area. So, if you’re a fuller-chest girl like myself, still sizing up would be your best route.

While the After Dark Collection is currently sold out, there likely will be a restock because of how popular the coats are. Until then, here are a few other KHY selects and faux-fur favorites I’ve been eyeing that you can shop right now.

It also comes in three firmness options—plush soft, luxury firm, and firm—making it a versatile choice for different sleep positions.   • From its conception, author Suzanne Collins taught young readers how to have hope in the face of destruction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, back in the days of going to the bookstore at midnight to get a fresh book, young fans flocked to their nearest bookstores waiting to see if Katniss Everdeen chose Peeta Mellark or Gale Hawthorne in the hit YA trilogy The Hunger Games. Remember the Borders parties and how many of us would rock a Katniss braid? Those were the days! But the franchise has always been more than a typical young adult series.

From its conception, author Suzanne Collins taught young readers how to have hope in the face of destruction. President Coriolanus Snow wanted the world to fall at his feet and Katniss Everdeen taught audiences to fight back. Still, in the midst of her quest to free the citizens of Panem, a love story was present and it is something that made Suzanne's novels (and the subsequent movies) special.

The main love triangle of the original run of books and films centered around Katniss Everdeen and her love for both Gale Hawthorne and Peeta Mellark. While the question of who Katniss will choose loomed over the story as our beloved heroes fought for their lives, it felt like the one topic that fans talked about. “Are you Team Peeta or Team Gale?” Unless you were me. I was too busy crying over the death of Finnick Odair and how tragic his love story was. But, still, many of the other fans were focused on why either guy was best for Katniss. That doesn’t mean that was it though. There were other ships that called to us too.

It has been revealed that in the middle of all the reapings and rebellions, fans realized one pairing had a different kind of history: Haymitch Abernathy and Effie Trinket. The two never had an explicit romance. Instead, the subtext between Effie and Haymitch led many fans to hope that there was a world where they would find love together. But their first meeting, as seen in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, is not where their will-they-won’t-they love story started. Instead, the prequel taught us more about Haymitch prior to his time in the arena and made it clear that the winner of the second Quarter Quell is one of the franchise’s best love interests.

Recent findings suggest that this time played by Joseph Zada, fans finally got a glimpse into the love story that broke him. Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak) was a Covey girl, a group of nomadic musicians that fans were first introduced to in the prequel novel and film The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. Haymitch fell in love with her prior to the start of Sunrise on the Reaping, even throwing himself in the line of fire to protect her, leading to him being forced to participate in the second Quarter Quell.

Like many other fans, in the original run of The Hunger Games, I wanted to know about Haymitch’s game. Mainly because we knew he survived by defeating double the amount of tributes that Katniss and Peeta did. It broke something in him. Or so we thought.

Recent findings suggest that during the first trilogy, Haymitch was a drunk, seemingly uncaring about the tributes he was meant to mentor. But I saw something deeper in him, a sadness and loneliness that no one was willing to talk to him about—not that Haymitch would open up anyway. For years, we thought it was the turmoil of the games themselves that sent him into a spiral. Through Sunrise on the Reaping, we got insight into how Haymitch went from a young District 12 boy who actually swore off drinking to the lonely man that Peeta and Katniss encounter during their games. In fact, it’s the same reason why Haymitch actually might be the best love interest in the entire franchise (and yes, that does include the lover boy Finnick Odair himself): His dedication to Lenore Dove.

There is a deep love that all of the characters in The Hunger Games have for their chosen ones. But Haymitch’s dedication to Lenore Dove is rooted in his own grief, loneliness, and fear of hurting someone else he loves.

President Snow’s continued hatred of District 12 didn’t just reignite with Katniss. Instead, the ripples of his lost romance with Lucy Gray Baird (originally seen in The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes) were thrown back in his face when Haymitch tried to break the games he was a part of. It meant that Snow had to send Haymitch a message and he did so in the most devastating way. Snow has Haymitch’s family killed and uses Haymitch’s own gift to Lenore Dove against him. All Haymitch wanted was to protect his family; instead they burn down his house with his family trapped inside and he was forced to hold his one true love in his arms as she died from the poison she unknowingly ingested that was hidden in the candy she thought Haymitch bought her. It’s no wonder why Haymitch isolates himself. He does so so that no one can be hurt by what the Capitol was willing to do to those he loved.

After seeing Sunrise on the Reaping, fans might think that Haymitch is actually more closely related to Finnick Odair in how they both show their love for someone by protecting them in any way possible. Still, Haymitch’s anguish over Lenore Dove kept him alone and separated from the rest of District 12 out of love. Finnick and Mags went into the game during Catching Fire because they both were protecting Annie. Haymitch isolated and drank himself into a stupor for the same reason.

According to recent reports, what can I say? I love two boys who are willing to hurt themselves to keep others safe. And aren’t going to just paint their faces to blend into foliage. (I’m so sorry, Peeta. I do love you, I promise!).

In many ways, Haymitch is the very definition of a “lover boy.” One who loved so deeply that the loss of it changed who he was. Still, the beauty of it shows why Haymitch was so cautious about caring for other people. He wasn’t cold or broken, he was afraid of what President Snow would do to those around him.

Seeing how Haymitch was before the Second Quarter Quell and what he was willing to do for his love of Lenore Dove? It set the standard for what a love interest was willing to do much higher than before. It also means that Peeta Mellark needs to step up his game if he wants to get on Haymitch’s level. “If not for the baby,” isn’t going to cut it when Haymitch is ready to take down an entire empire for love.

Industry observers note that birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays are still hard for Fieri, but he’s also found some comfort in his family. In a 2024 interview with Graham Bensinger, he said, “The funny thing is, out of everything that's happened, it has made me probably 10 times closer to my mom.”.

But his historic win is not all the internet has been talking about. At his celebratory Election Night event in Austin, Texas, the 37-year-old senator-elect was joined by his girlfriend, Brianna Menard, who was previously his chief of staff. Days later, the two attended a University of Texas football game—to which Menard wore a corduroy minidress she thrifted the week before—and the moment went viral across social media. (Even better, Talarico’s mom was the one who shared the photo of the couple at the game that rapidly got traction on X.).

Chalk it up to her political prowess, clear sense of style, or the fact that she looks like an Instagram baddie, but some fans have even gone as far as to declare the pair this generation’s John F. Kennedy and Jacqueline Kennedy.

The couple first met in 2022, when Menard joined the politician’s team as chief of staff, and their relationship eventually turned romantic. Menard has been by Talarico’s side throughout his Senate campaign, accompanying him to the polls on Election Day in November and later joining him onstage to celebrate his historic victory.

So, who is Brianna Menard? Ahead, everything to know about Talarico’s accomplished and stylish girlfriend.

According to recent reports, menard is a born-and-raised Texan. She attended and graduated from the University of Texas at Austin, where she studied government.

In 2022, Menard was hired as Talarico’s chief of staff. According to reports, the two didn’t begin dating until a year later, after which Menard left her role working for the politician. In August 2026, Talarico’s campaign confirmed the couple’s relationship. “Four years ago, after he and his then-chief of staff developed feelings for each other and started dating, she left the office to pursue other opportunities,” a Talarico campaign spokesman told the New York Times.

Recent findings suggest that after leaving Talarico’s office, Menard worked on the campaign for Rep. Salman Bhojani, the first Muslim member of the Texas legislature, and eventually became his chief of staff.

It has been revealed that menard is presently the director of TEXPAC and political education at the Texas Medical Association. According to her bio on the organization’s site, before stepping into the role, she had a decade of experience working in the Texas Legislature and previously served as executive director of the Early Childhood Caucus of the Texas House, where she led bipartisan efforts to “advance early learning, childcare access, workforce development, and healthcare affordability.”.

Menard’s bio also lists her as the Board Secretary for Wheatsville Food Co-op and a member of the City of Austin’s Early Childhood Council.

According to a now-deleted bio on the Wheatsville Food Co-Op site, where she presently serves as Board Secretary, Menard called herself a “foodie and a committed vegan” who loves cooking. In the welcome post, she also revealed her love of yoga, dancing, and cuddling her cat named Zia.

“I’ve spent my career serving in the Texas Legislature and working on political campaigns across the state with the goal of making Texas a healthier and more equitable home for all of us,” she wrote in the post.

Menard joined Talarico at the polls to vote early in the midterm elections. On November 3, she also joined Talarico’s Election Night event in Austin, where she congratulated the Senator-elect on stage following his historic win. The couple shared a sweet hug and kiss to celebrate.

Recent findings suggest that thanksgiving is around the corner, which means it's time for too much turkey, naps facedown on the floor while everyone begs you to help with the dishes, at least one relative saying something problematic, and texting your hometown ex to "see how they are." In other words, it's the coziest time of year! And if you're looking to amp up said cozy vibes by a factor of ten, we highly recommend crawling into bed (and/or some sort of wearable blanket situation) and firing up anywhere from 1-10 (or 40) iconic Thanksgiving episodes of television.

There's truly something for everyone on this list—whether you want to watch every single Friends Thanksgiving episode, enjoy the Thanksgiving misadventures of Bob Belcher, or kick back with a classic Thanksgiving episode of Gossip Girl. Because yes, there are multiple.

It has been revealed that oh, and if you like your Thanksgiving episodes dripping with wealth, there's also The Sopranos and Succession. No matter which ep(s) you press play on, we highly recommend enjoying them with a vodka cranberry in hand (counts as cranberry sauce, fight me), as well as a full pumpkin pie. What happens between you and said pumpkin pie is your business! Happy Thanksgiving to one and all!

If your family makes a point of watching the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade every year, you'll appreciate the suitably wacky plotline in this classic Seinfeld episode. In the days leading up to Turkey Day, Kramer gives away all of Jerry's shoes, George attempts to purchase a car once owned by Jon Voight, and Elaine gets her boss a ticket to pilot the Woody the Woodpecker balloon at NYC's famous parade.

No Thanksgiving is complete without an episode of Bob's Burgers, and this one takes the cake for its hilarious depiction of meal prep gone wrong (read: Bob's turkey finds its way—mysteriously—to the toilet).

In this hilarious episode of Fresh Off the Boat, Jessica finally gets the chance to prove to her mother that she can handle the Thanksgiving meal. Of course, nothing's ever that easy in a sitcom, and getting something on the table proves nearly impossible.

In a recent development, mindy attends Thanksgiving dinner at her friend Gwen's, where she encounters her worst nightmare in the form of her former blind date, Dennis, and his new Indian girlfriend. Thankfully, Mindy always knows what to say—and she never holds back.

Industry observers note that it wouldn't be a rerun binge without a dose of Cheers, right? In this Thanksgiving classic, most of the crew have no place to go for the holiday, so they throw a potluck at Carla's. But an uncooked turkey, a frustrated Frasier, and last min changes to the guest list throw the day into disarray.

Thanksgiving is practically synonymous with football, and Friday Night Lights, naturally, leans all the way in. The gang gets together for a feast ahead of the big Friday night game, and it's up to Landry to make the game-winning field goal.

It has been revealed that PLL is not necessarily the cheery holiday fare you're used to on Thanksgiving Day, but if you need a captivating tale to distract you while the pies bake, this episode is perfect. There's holiday decorating, pumpkin pie-making...and, oh, murder!

Industry observers note that so this isn't technically a Thanksgiving episode, but the Harvest Festival is the closest the Parks and Rec crew gets to celebrating Turkey Day onscreen. Plus, a "curse" is involved.

It has been revealed that after learning about class divisions in Rwanda at school, Cory and Shawn decide to be progressive and bridge the gap between their own socioeconomic statuses by...uh, having Thanksgiving at the Hunters' trailer park? Sure!

According to recent reports, when Will's mom, Viola, arrives in Bel-Air for Thanksgiving, she causes a fuss when she criticizes Vivian for letting the kids be lazy during the holiday. Hurt, Vivian makes the kids cook Thanksgiving dinner, which—surprise, surprise—turns into a hilarious, but heartwarming, disaster.

Danger's always lurking around the corner in Riverdale, even on Thanksgiving Day. An ice storm forces the community into lockdown, and when Archie decides to throw a feast for underprivileged kids, some unexpected guests arrive.

Industry observers note that blair Waldorf is the HBIC of Thanksgiving, and that's a fact. Although every single season of Gossip Girl serves us a delicious Thanksgiving episode, season 1 sets the bar high with flashbacks of Serena drunk (in broad daylight) the year before, a look into Blair's past, and the reveal of Rufus and Lily's v. complicated history.

This Thanksgiving episode of Grey's Anatomy might be the most relatable television to ever exist. Izzie wants to have the perfect Turkey Day, but she is literally clueless and has no idea what to do. I mean, you can’t really blame her. This episode aired in 2005 and Pinterest wasn't even invented until 2010. How do you cook anything without Pinterest?

Industry observers note that dwight deals with some childhood trauma the only way he knows how...by creating an elaborate hay festival so he can finally be crowned Hay King. Also, Ryan tries to scam everyone out of a ton of money. Festive!

There are 10 Thanksgiving episodes of Friends, but this one is the best, thanks to Monica, Joey, Chandler, Phoebe, Rachel, and Ross sitting around sharing their holiday horror stories. Comedic gold.

Ahh, nothing makes you realize your crazy family isn't so awful like spending Thanksgiving in solitary confinement or eating dinner with a spork. Right, Piper and Alex?

Rory and Lorelai attend FOUR Turkey Day feasts, which actually sounds like a total nightmare given the fact that they had to wear real clothes and couldn't take post-meal naps on the couch.

Recent findings suggest that everyone's trying to either skip out on dinner, avoid dressing up, or troll each other's ability to cook. Basically, it's the Modern Family crew living out your absolute best Thanksgiving dreams.

Sources indicate that there's really only one reason to watch this, and it's Uncle Jesse (in all his first-season, borderline-mullet glory) cooking a turkey in a leather vest. Enjoy!

In which Jacqueline notes she's thankful for "loving someone other than herself…and revenge," which honestly, we should all aspire to.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ever since the NFL season kicked off back in September, the Minnesota Vikings’ star receiver Justin Jefferson has been going full-tilt. Last night, his team squared off against the San Fransisco 49ers in Mexico City (the NFL has been scheduling more away-gamers outside the U.S. to try to expand their viewership) in one of the marquee matchups of the season, and while the 49ers ended up winning that one, Jefferson remains inspired by the Vikings’ 7-3 record so far. “I’ve been great,” Jefferson notes. “Everything’s been going really well, and I’m feeling good.”.

Sources indicate that preparing for such a big game is no small feat, of course—even if a pro like Jefferson makes it look easy. Ahead of hitting the field, you can often find him getting ready both physically and mentally. “Preparation is everything: I want to make sure I'm confident, focused, and ready to perform at my best,” he claims. How did he prepare for Mexico City? “A big part has been making sure I'm physically and mentally ready for the challenges of playing at a higher altitude,” Jefferson says. (Mexico City is about 1.4 miles above sea level—much more intense than even Denver’s Mile High Stadium.) “I've been using the altitude chamber to help my body acclimate. Mentally, it’s about studying the plays, understanding the different schemes, and making sure we're approaching the game with the right mindset.”.

Industry observers note that A more unexpected way Jefferson gets game-day ready, however: With his intentional tunnel-walk outfits. Yesterday, before the athletes even hit the field, Jefferson wanted to rock a meaningful look that would put him in the right mindset for his Mexico City matchup—so he enlisted one of the city’s most well-known designers, Patricio Campillo, to craft a custom look for him. “I've always tried to make my tunnel looks reflect where I am in the world, especially when we're playing internationally,” says Jefferson. “For me, fashion is an opportunity to connect with different cultures and showcase designers who bring something unique to the table.”.

A very cool moment for me: Meet the designer—Patricio Campillo—behind the look.

Wanting to rep a design that represented the local culture, Jefferson called up Campillo to start ideating his custom look. He was drawn to the designer for his unique craftsmanship, creativity, and attention to detail. “Choosing Campillo felt like a natural decision—I was genuinely impressed,” says Jefferson. “You can tell how much time, passion, and hard work goes into creating these looks. Being able to represent that craftsmanship on an international stage is something I think is really special.”.

Sources indicate that together, they landed on doing a cool, modern take on tailoring. Campillo created a cropped, boxy-style jacket with brown leather trousers—a signature element of the label that the designer wanted to introduce to a whole new audience. “It’s exciting to see someone of Justin’s caliber embrace Campillo,” he claims. “I’ve always believed that fashion has the power to bring together people from different backgrounds, so seeing an athlete like Justin connect with our work is especially meaningful.”.

He accessorized with pieces such as a horsehair bag, Oakley shades, and his signature chains. When the wide receiver put on the final look for the first ime, he was immediately drawn to the finer details. “One of my favorite details was the horsehair incorporated into the bag,” says Jefferson. “It’s such a unique touch and gives the piece a lot of character.” He also appreciated the hand-craftsmanship. “Knowing how much time and effort goes into creating each piece makes you appreciate the look even more,” he says. “I love wearing things that have a story behind them, and this outfit definitely does.”.

The fit, custom made by Patricio Campillo.

It’s not the first time that Jefferson has flexed a fashion statement for his tunnel walk. During past games, he has worn everything from Off-White to Louis Vuitton and Chrome Hearts. What he wears and experiments, of course, depends on the setting. “My tunnel looks are really an extension of my personality, and how I’m feeling that day,” he notes. “There are a few things I consider when putting a look together: my mood, who we’re playing, and the brands or designers I want to showcase. Fashion has become another creative outlet for me, and I enjoy stepping outside of what people might expect.”.

It has been revealed that this fluid approach to dressing applies to his off-duty wardrobe, too. Jefferson indicates he enjoys playing around with fashion even on his days off. “Right now, I'd describe my personal style as evolving,” he says. “I'm really focused on experimenting with different looks and exploring styles I might not have considered earlier in my career. I like stepping out of my comfort zone and being open to trying new things. Fashion is all about self-expression, and I think the more willing you are to take risks, the more you learn about yourself and what you like.”.

Recent findings suggest that what does this mean for the rest of Jefferson’s NFL season? You can expect tons more tunnel-walk outfits, for starters. “Every week is another opportunity to bring something exciting to the tunnel,” he notes. “We love finding ways to surprise people, turn heads, and keep things interesting.” Start taking your bets—fashion bets, not sporting bets—on what runway outfit or custom creation he will don next. “We’ve already had a few outfits this season that have gotten a lot of attention, and that’s always fun to see,” he says. “But for me, it’s not just about getting people talking—it’s about continuing to discover newly introduced brands, experimenting with different styles, and finding creative ways to express myself through fashion.”.

You May Be Thawing Your Turkey Wrong—Here’s How To Avoid Spreading Salmonella

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (673 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Delish

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thanksgiving is a marathon, not a sprint.
  • Industry observers note that frozen turkeys are generally the more accessible and affordable option.
  • Making sure it tastes good is one thing, but ensuring that it's safe to eat is something else entirely.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanksgiving is a marathon, not a sprint. And the most involved, time-consuming dish is undoubtedly the turkey. The centerpiece of your holiday table needs hours in the oven and at least a day of brining, but don't forget the time it takes to defrost beforehand, too.

Industry observers note that frozen turkeys are generally the more accessible and affordable option. But they do require a little extra TLC and planning. So if you buy a frozen bird this year, you'll need to know how to work with it.

Making sure it tastes good is one thing, but ensuring that it's safe to eat is something else entirely. Like chicken, turkey can spread Salmonella and other harmful bacteria. You should exercise caution at every stage of the process, including thawing, to avoid making your guests sick. Here’s what you should know.

Recent findings suggest that the USDA says it's also safe to defrost turkey in cold water, but in our opinion, it's not worth the hassle. The best bet is to thaw it in the refrigerator, where the bird can gradually defrost at the safe temperature with less risk of bacterial growth. What you should never do: thaw it on the counter, in the garage, or with warm water.

Sources indicate that these environments are less controlled and can expose the turkey to the temperature danger zone (between 40°F and 140°F), where germs grow rapidly. Even if the center of the turkey is still frozen, the thawed exterior can become a hotbed for Salmonella by the time you're ready to roast.

Roasted turkey drippings make great gravy. But raw turkey juice dripping all over your fridge? Not so much. Even shrink-wrapped birds can leak, so you should always store your turkey on a baking sheet or roasting pan while it thaws.

Food safety experts also recommend storing raw meat on the lowest shelf. That way, any leaks are less likely to drip onto other ingredients in your fridge.

Sources indicate that we know you're probably keeping a lot of other ingredients in your fridge, so it can be hard to set aside extra room for the turkey. That mentioned, it's a step worth doing. Giving your turkey plenty of personal space minimizes the risk of raw meat or its juices coming into contact with other ingredients.

Sources indicate that in the event that your turkey does contaminate another ingredient, here's what to know: Foods that won’t be cooked, like salad greens, should be tossed if they’ve come into contact with raw turkey juices. Cooking contaminated foods thoroughly can kill harmful bacteria, but you’ll also need to clean any surfaces the juices touched.

In a recent development, turkeys are massive, so they take a long time to thaw all the way through. The experts at Butterball say you should allocate a day for every four pounds of turkey if you're keeping it in the fridge. That means if you're working with a 16-pound bird, set aside four days just for defrosting. Once it's fully thawed, Butterball claims your turkey will stay safe in the fridge for up to four days.

Sources indicate that and on top of that, brining can make your turkey even more flavorful. If your frozen bird didn’t come pre-seasoned, consider setting aside another day or two for that step. (Want some guidance? Check out our brining guide.).

It’s extremely important to keep things clean while you’re handling a turkey. One of the most common ways Salmonella spreads in the kitchen is through cross-contamination caused by poor hygiene.

It has been revealed that so wash those hands (including under your fingernails!) with soap and water for at least 20 seconds. Make sure you also thoroughly clean any utensils and surfaces that come into contact with raw turkey or its juices using hot, soapy water.

And above all, don’t stress! Americans prepare millions of turkeys every Thanksgiving, so you're not alone in your turkey-roasting journey. Follow the tips above to ensure yours turns out safe to eat and delicious.

#192091. PDRN—AKA Salmon Sperm—Is the Buzziest Skincare Ingredient of the Year. Should You Use It, Though?
