PDRN—AKA Salmon Sperm—Is the Buzziest Skincare Ingredient of the Year. Should You Use It, Though?

📅 02 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
  • Industry observers note that would you slather salmon sperm on your face?
  • Before you freak, it’s not like skincare products have raw salmon sperm in them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

Industry observers note that would you slather salmon sperm on your face? TBH, you might already be. PDRN has been one of the buzziest skincare ingredients of the year, and its prevalence is thanks to the Korean skincare boom. Dermatologists think that this ingredient is only going to become more popular, too. "PDRN has real staying power because there are decades of science-based research that is supported by medical use, which gives it credibility,” states Melda Isaac, MD.

Before you freak, it’s not like skincare products have raw salmon sperm in them. (That would be a serious health violation.) I sought to understand the ingredient a bit more, and the science is interesting. PDRN might just be the coolest ingredient, like ever. Intrigued? Well, you’re in the right place. Keep reading to learn everything you need to know about PDRN.

PDRN, or polydeoxyribonucleotide, "are DNA fragments derived from sperm cells of certain trout or, more commonly in skincare, salmon," claims Dr. Isaac. So, yeah, you technically are slathering the sperm of a lil salmon on your face. But don't worry, Dr. Isaac confirms that the extracted sperm is filtered to remove impurities, then sterilized so that it's suitable for topical use.

Recent findings suggest that why sperm, though? "Studies indicate that salmon sperm are the most suitable source for the extraction of highly purified DNA without the risk of impurities due to their low levels of proteins, peptides, and other contaminants compared to other DNA sources," says Dr. Isaac.

PDRN is fantastic for a variety of skin concerns, especially regenerating tissue and cell renewal, which helps skin become more resilient, elastic, firmer, and smoother. Basically, it can help stimulate collagen production, improve skin texture and tone, make pores look tighter, and reduce fine lines and wrinkles.

According to recent reports, to get science-y, "it works primarily by activating adenosine A2A receptors, which are crucial in anti-inflammatory effects," shares Dr. Isaac. It's largely used to "promote cell growth and repair and enhance the skin’s natural healing process, making it an ideal component for post-treatment recovery," she adds. But it can also inhibit melanin production to help reduce hyperpigmentation, making it great for getting rid of acne scars and sun spots.

According to recent reports, PDRN isn’t just found in topical products. Some people opt to get PDRN injections at med spas and doctor’s offices. The biggest difference between what you get during a professional treatment versus what’s in a skincare formula is the concentration. PDRN that's injected into skin during a procedure at a derm's office is much more potent than what you'd find in Hailey Bieber's favorite Medicube PDRN Collagen Gel Mask.

Recent findings suggest that it's also key to keep in mind that PDRN products differ when it comes to strength and in how they were manufactured. Dr. Isaac urges you to consider if the product contains salmon DNA or trout DNA (as this can potentially change the efficacy and strength of results), plus where the salmon is coming from (was it farm-raised or freshly caught from pure streams or rivers, she notes).

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to at-home formulas, Dr. Isaac is pro-PDRN in basically all forms. Most of all, she recommends choosing something that you can be consistent with. "Serums are designed for daily use and long-term maintenance, while masks provide an immediate boost since they are left on the skin longer, allowing ingredients to soak in," she explains. Adding a PDRN serum, like VT Cosmetics PDRN 100 Essence Serum, to your nighttime skincare routine is often the easiest option. Or incorporate it with a weekly overnight mask (I've been loving Abib PDRN Collagen Overnight Mask for my acne-prone skin) or a PDRN sheet mask. "In the treatment room, I think PDRN masks are a great addition to post-laser care as they offer immediate soothing properties and improve downtime or recovery period," she adds.

According to recent reports, dr. Isaac recommends combining at-home treatments with your in-office procedures to double up on your results. FWIW, her go-to product at-home is LúmEnvy Glass Skin Brightening Serum, which she finds helps expedite the skin's healing process after cosmetic treatments, as well as improves skin luminosity and texture. Contributing beauty editor, Mary Honkus, can attest to this. She used the Medicube PDRN Pink Collagen Capsule Cream post laser-facial, and her skin healed much faster than her dermatologist said it would—legit in less than a week.

The best thing about PDRN is that it's gentle and effective for all skin types, including sensitive, notes Dr. Isaac. "It doesn’t strip or over-correct, making it safe across the board," she states. In fact, you can even use it with actives—including retinol, growth factors, AHAs, BHAs, and vitamin C—to help reduce irritation.

One thing to keep in mind: Proceed with caution if you have a fish or shellfish allergy, Dr. Isaac warns. Talk to your doctor before you start using a product just to be sure it won't cause irritation (and of course, any fresh product you add into your routine puts you at risk for some irritation, even if you don't think you're allergic to it). There is usually a lot of purification done with these formulas, but an allergic response could possibly happen, so it's best to be safe.

It has been revealed that while rubbing salmon sperm on your skin might sound a lil freaky, it's actually backed by science to help smooth and tighten. Who woulda thought? While an in-office facial using PDRN might lead to quicker and more noticeable results, at-home topical masks, serums, and creams are also pretty effective and compound results over time. "It truly is one of those rare ingredients that transcends hydration, repair, and renewal universally," notes Dr. Isaac.

As for what the future holds for salmon sperm, Dr. Isaac is convinced we're just getting started. "I think there will be increased concentrations of the active ingredients, more combinations of PDRN with other rejuvenating products, and there will be more options in delivery mechanisms, including injections of PDRN into deeper tissues," she notes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During her three-day tour of India, the Princess of Wales attended the 2026 Earthshot Prize Ceremony in Mumbai. Prince William founded the initiative in 2020, and it awards environmental solutions with grants to scale and advance their projects.

For the event, Kate wore an oxblood, floor-length Anarkali dress by designer Mahima Mahajan and paired it with extra-fluffy, voluminous bohemian curls pinned in a half-updo.

According to recent reports, an elegant, extra-glossy wavy hairstyle has long been a beauty signature for the princess, often teamed with a side part, hats, or a polished ponytail. But for the green carpet in India, the royal opted for a much more dramatic style that matches the glamorous mood of her outfit, with tighter, cascading bohemian curls woven into a beautiful half-updo twist for a romantic finish.

"I would create these curls using a medium-sized tong," recommends Philipp Haug, co-founder of Haug London Haus salon. "Take relatively small sections and use the tongs with a twisting technique, curling one section away from the face and alternating with one section towards the face throughout. Slightly root stretch when you come to the top of the head instead of curling too close to the scalp.".

To enhance the fluffiness and volume of the curls, shake them out with your fingers instead of combing them.

Your next special occasion hair inspiration, sorted.
